claude_md.overview: claudegen is a cli project written in rust.
claude_md.architecture:
- `src/pipeline/` - Core generation pipeline with phases (project detection, module detection, skill detection, constraint extraction, convention inference), quality assessment, consensus, refinement, and artifact generation
- `src/cli/` - Command-line interface with subcommands (init, generate, validate, sync, status, clean, config) and user interaction
- `src/analyzer/` - Code analysis with multi-language parsers (Rust, Go, TypeScript, Python, Bash) and file scanning with gitignore support
- `src/ai/` - AI provider abstraction (Claude, OpenAI) with circuit breaker, chain-of-thought, budget tracking, and response validation
- `src/utils/` - Utility functions for path handling, pattern matching, and tool helpers
- `src/config/` - Configuration loading and types for project settings
- `src/constants.rs` - Global constants and configuration defaults
- `src/types/` - Core domain types for artifacts (skills, agents, rules), validation, errors, graph nodes/edges, and insights
- `src/storage/` - Persistent storage for generation state and caching

- TOML Configuration Pattern: TOML-based hierarchical configuration with sections for project metadata, analysis settings, and glob-based file filtering (see @.claudegen/config.toml:1)

- Event Sourcing with ULID-based Sessions: Sessions organized in directories named by ULID, containing event streams as JSONL files (see @.claudegen/sessions/01KGF1768NR4ECESGM669H622T/events.jsonl:1)

- Tagged Event Payload Structure: Events follow tagged union pattern with event_type discriminator and payload containing type-specific data (see @.claudegen/sessions/01KGF1768NR4ECESGM669H622T/events.jsonl:1)
- PID-based Lock File Pattern: JSON lock file with PID and timestamp for advisory file locking across processes (see @.claudegen/.lock:1)
- Rust dependency caching pattern: All jobs use Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with cache-on-failure: true to persist cargo cache even when build fails (see @.github/workflows/ci.yml:28)
- Cross-platform release matrix: Build matrix covers 4 targets: x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux (via cross), aarch64-darwin, x86_64-windows (see @.github/workflows/release.yml:17)
- Nextest for test execution: Uses cargo-nextest instead of cargo test for faster parallel test execution (see @.github/workflows/ci.yml:34)
- Platform-specific archive format: Release archives are tar.gz for Unix and zip for Windows, with SHA256 checksums (see @.github/workflows/release.yml:56)
- Clippy warnings as errors: Strict clippy enforcement with -D warnings flag fails build on any warning (see @.github/workflows/ci.yml:124)

- Hierarchical Config Resolution: Configuration is loaded by merging multiple sources in priority order: defaults → global (~/.config/claudegen/) → project (.claudegen/) → env vars (CLAUDEGEN_*). Each layer overrides the previous. (see @src/config/loader.rs:30)

- Multi-level Validation with Cross-field Checks: Config types implement validate() methods that check both single-field constraints and cross-field dependencies. Root Config.validate() orchestrates validation order. (see @src/config/types.rs:81)

- Builder-style Defaults with Serde: Default trait implementations provide sensible defaults, #[serde(default)] enables partial config files, and explicit default functions (default_true, default_module_agent_threshold) handle specific field defaults. (see @src/config/types.rs:57)

- Type-Loader Separation: Config types are separated from loading logic. types.rs defines data structures, loader.rs handles I/O and merging. ConfigLoader is a unit struct with only static methods. (see @src/config/mod.rs:1)

- Weighted Multi-dimensional Scoring: ValueConfig calculates overall quality scores from three dimensions (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness) using configurable weights that must sum to 1.0 (see @src/config/types.rs:302)

- Parser Trait Pattern: All language parsers implement a common Parser trait with parse() and language() methods, enabling polymorphic parser selection and consistent error handling. (see @src/analyzer/parser/traits.rs:36)

- Language Metadata Table: Language metadata uses a macro-based table (lang_meta!) that centralizes display names, highlight strings, extensions, aliases, and parser support flags. (see @src/analyzer/parser/language.rs:30)

- Factory Functions for AST Nodes: Helper functions (create_file_node, create_code_node, create_code_edge, evidence_from_node) reduce boilerplate in parser implementations. (see @src/analyzer/parser/traits.rs:69)

- Tree-sitter Query Pattern: Tree-sitter queries are defined as string literals and executed via Query::new + QueryCursor pattern consistently across all parsers. (see @src/analyzer/parser/rust_lang.rs:62)
- Compiled Pattern Sets: FileScanner pre-compiles glob patterns at construction time with fast-path detection for '**/*' pattern. (see @src/analyzer/scanner/file_scanner.rs:72)
- Error Context Enrichment: Parser errors include path context by mutating ClaudegenError::Parse path field after initial creation. (see @src/analyzer/parser/go.rs:23)
- Builder Pattern with Method Chaining: Builder pattern with method chaining for constructing complex objects - returns Self for fluent API (see @src/pipeline/analysis/corpus.rs:29)

- Tiered Classification System: Three-tier finding classification: Tier1 (generic/rejected), Tier2 (project conventions), Tier3 (high-value hidden knowledge) (see @src/pipeline/analysis/finding.rs:191)
- Structured LLM Response Deserialization: LLM responses are deserialized through deserialize_llm_response helper with context for error messages (see @src/pipeline/analysis/distributed.rs:269)
- Bounded Parallel Execution: Semaphore-bounded parallel execution with JoinSet for concurrent chunk analysis (see @src/pipeline/analysis/distributed.rs:137)
- Extract-Validate-Corpus Pipeline: Raw findings extracted from chunks flow through validation to become ValidatedFindings in a corpus (see @src/pipeline/analysis/extractor.rs:12)

- Reference Validation with Graduated Status: References validated against file registry with graduated status: Valid, FileLevelOnly, DirectoryOnly, FileNotFound, LineOutOfRange (see @src/pipeline/analysis/finding.rs:147)
- Schema-Driven LLM Prompts: Analysis types use JsonSchema derive for automatic LLM schema generation via generate_schema::<T>() (see @src/pipeline/analysis/distributed.rs:311)
- Shared type aliases with Arc: Types like SharedBudget, SharedMetrics, SharedProvider use Arc wrapper types for thread-safe sharing across async tasks (see @src/ai/budget.rs:114)

- Circuit breaker for provider resilience: Circuit breaker pattern prevents cascading failures by tracking consecutive failures and blocking requests when threshold exceeded (see @src/ai/provider/circuit_breaker.rs:1)
- Lock-free atomics with CAS for budget tracking: AtomicU64 with Acquire/Release ordering for counters, RwLock for complex state with poisoned lock recovery (see @src/ai/budget.rs:47)
- Tiered provider routing by phase: ProviderSet routes requests to different model tiers (fast/default/performance) based on pipeline phase (see @src/ai/provider/mod.rs:135)
- Partial parsing with graceful degradation: parse_partial attempts full deserialization first, then falls back to field-by-field with defaults for failed fields (see @src/ai/response/partial.rs:15)
- Model registry with capability lookup: ModelRegistry provides model-specific context windows with alias resolution and auth-mode-aware extended context (see @src/ai/model_capabilities.rs:165)
- Tracked provider wrapper for metrics/budget: TrackedProvider wraps any LlmProvider to enforce budget limits and record metrics automatically (see @src/ai/provider/tracked.rs:16)
- Schema transformation for strict structured output: transform_for_strict adds additionalProperties:false and converts oneOf to Claude-compatible formats (see @src/ai/response/schema.rs:35)

- Three-Layer Analysis Architecture: Three-layer architecture for analysis: Extraction → Validation → Projection, with clear separation between raw findings, validated findings, and final output types (see @src/pipeline/analysis/mod.rs:12)

- Trait-Based Generic Merge Pattern: Generic trait-based merging with MergeKey trait for simple cases, specialized implementations for complex types requiring internal merge logic (see @src/pipeline/analysis/merger.rs:21)

- Oscillation Detection Pattern: Oscillation detection using hash-based proposal history and confidence snapshot comparison to prevent infinite analysis loops (see @src/pipeline/analysis/reanalysis.rs:126)
- Durable Execution with Checkpoints: Checkpoint-based crash recovery with atomic writes, lock files for process detection, and event sourcing for audit trails (see @src/pipeline/checkpoint.rs:1)
- Verified Reference Pool Pattern: Pool of verified file:line references validated against actual file contents to prevent LLM hallucination (see @src/pipeline/analysis/reference_pool.rs:1)
- Distributed Analysis with Chunk Checkpointing: Distributed analysis with chunk-level checkpointing for recovery, map-reduce aggregation of results (see @src/pipeline/checkpoint.rs:98)
- Module Re-export Facade Pattern: Re-export pattern in mod.rs providing clean public API while hiding internal module structure (see @src/pipeline/analysis/mod.rs:30)
- Bounded Collection with FIFO Eviction: Bounded collection pattern using VecDeque with explicit max_size and pop_front/push_back for FIFO eviction (see @src/pipeline/consensus/types.rs:196)
- Two-Pass Validation Pattern: Two-pass validation combining programmatic checks (100% reliable) with LLM semantic checks for quality judgment (see @src/pipeline/deep_review.rs:155)
- Event Sourcing for Resumable State: Event sourcing pattern with JSONL append-only log for state reconstruction via event replay (see @src/pipeline/events/store.rs:1)
- Incremental State Compaction: Incremental compaction to reduce state size while preserving recovery capability (see @src/pipeline/events/compaction.rs:37)
- Multi-Strategy Path Resolution: 6-step path resolution strategy for handling various project structures and path formats (see @src/pipeline/file_reference.rs:124)
- Layered Agent Generation: Three-layer agent generation: base agents always generated, module specialists and domain experts conditional (see @src/pipeline/generation/agents/mod.rs:26)
- Semantic Constraint Routing: Semantic routing of constraints and patterns to relevant agents/skills via GenerationContext (see @src/pipeline/generation/agents/base.rs:18)
- Weighted Multi-Dimension Scoring: Weighted dimension scoring with configurable thresholds for convergence detection (see @src/pipeline/feedback.rs:68)
- Consensus with Veto Power: Consensus with veto power for critical agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts) (see @src/pipeline/consensus/types.rs:167)
- Builder Pattern for Context Assembly: Builder pattern with with_* methods for optional context enrichment returning Self for chaining (see @src/pipeline/generation/context.rs:156)

- Priority-Ordered Rule Hierarchy: Hierarchical rule generation with priority-based ordering (100=project, 90=tech, 85=framework, 80=module, 75=domain, 70=group) (see @src/pipeline/generation/rules/mod.rs:45)
- Validation Result with Warnings: Three-tier validation result pattern: Pass, PassWithWarnings, Fail with score and issues list (see @src/pipeline/generation/artifact/validators.rs:15)
- Project-Size-Adaptive Configuration: Tiered configuration gates with thresholds adjusted by project size (minimal <10, small <50, default) (see @src/pipeline/generation/evidence_gate.rs:77)
- Test Context Factory Pattern: Test helper functions that construct minimal valid context objects for unit testing (see @src/pipeline/generation/agents/module.rs:130)

- Static-then-LLM validation pipeline: Static validation runs before LLM calls to catch deterministic issues (file refs, required sections) at zero cost, reducing unnecessary API calls (see @src/pipeline/quality/judge.rs:136)

- Signal-to-hint conversion for LLM validation: Detection signals are converted to hints with confidence levels (definitive/high/medium) for LLM interpretation rather than hard-coded decisions (see @src/pipeline/phases/project_detection.rs:83)

- Tiered dimension requirements for convergence: Quality dimensions have tiered requirements: core_passed (actionability+evidence), minimum_viable (actionability OR evidence), any_passed (any dimension) (see @src/pipeline/quality_assessment.rs:108)

- Known/Unknown enum for extensible issue codes: Issue codes use Known/Unknown enum pattern with From<&str> for flexible parsing while preserving type safety for known codes (see @src/pipeline/quality/issue_codes.rs:6)

- Adaptive parallel evaluation based on artifact count: Large artifact sets use chunked parallel evaluation (chunk_size=10) while small sets (<= 20) use full parallelism (see @src/pipeline/quality/judge.rs:215)

- Pattern-based file detection with const arrays: Detection uses pattern arrays for file matching (TEST_PATTERNS, AUTH_PATTERNS, etc.) enabling easy extension without code changes (see @src/pipeline/phases/skill_detection.rs:10)
- Layered artifact generation: Three-layer artifact generation: Base (always), Module (conditional on detection), Hierarchy (conditional on groups/domains) (see @README.md:1)
- Skills/Rules/Agents separation: Skills define HOW (methodology), Rules define WHAT (knowledge), Agents define WHO (role) (see @README.md:1)
- Figment-based configuration: Uses figment with TOML for configuration, supporting environment variable overrides (see @Cargo.toml:1)
- Multi-language parsing: Multiple tree-sitter parsers for TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go, and Bash (see @Cargo.toml:1)
- Release build optimization: Release profile optimized with LTO, single codegen unit, and stripping (see @Cargo.toml:1)
- Command dispatch pattern: CLI is structured as a main entry point that dispatches to subcommand modules. Each command lives in claudegen::cli::commands::{name} module. (see @src/main.rs:152)
- Custom Result type with error categories: Uses custom Result type from types::error module with ResultExt trait for enrichment. Errors propagate with ? operator. (see @src/main.rs:137)
- Selective re-export pattern: Public API is carefully curated in lib.rs through explicit re-exports. Internal modules are pub but specific types are selectively exposed. (see @src/lib.rs:19)
- Namespaced constants via nested modules: Constants are organized in nested modules (tools, llm, provider, validation, cli) for namespacing. (see @src/constants.rs:4)

- Tracing-based logging with CLI verbosity control: Uses tracing-subscriber with EnvFilter for configurable log levels. Supports --verbose (debug), --quiet (error), default (info). (see @src/main.rs:143)

- Artifact Reference to Path Mapping: ArtifactRef enum maps abstract artifact types to concrete file paths, providing single source of truth for output locations (see @src/pipeline/sync/dependencies.rs:27)

- Dependency Graph for Incremental Updates: DependencyGraph tracks file→module→artifact relationships to enable incremental regeneration based on what actually changed (see @src/pipeline/sync/dependencies.rs:44)
- Blake3-based Change Detection: FileTracker uses blake3 hashing to detect file changes efficiently without storing full content (see @src/pipeline/sync/tracker.rs:113)

- Deterministic vs Semantic Validation Split: Validation and quality assessment are separated: validation handles deterministic checks (duplicates, file existence), while LlmJudge handles semantic quality (see @src/pipeline/validation/simplified.rs:7)

- File Reference Validation Pattern: Evidence traceability validates file references in content against VerifiedFileRegistry, including optional line number bounds checking (see @src/pipeline/validation/simplified.rs:153)
- Re-export Pattern for Module APIs: Module re-exports types through mod.rs for clean public API while keeping implementation in separate files (see @src/pipeline/sync/mod.rs:12)

- Strategy pattern with rotator: Strategies implement RefinementStrategy trait with applicable_to(), priority(), and refine_* methods. StrategyRotator selects and tracks strategies based on history and escalation level (see @src/pipeline/strategy/mod.rs:161)

- Failure tracking with bounded retries: Refinement tracks artifact/strategy pairs that fail repeatedly. After max_failures (default 2), the pair is skipped. Success clears failure history. (see @src/pipeline/refinement/failure_tracker.rs:28)

- Selective judgment caching: RefinementState caches JudgmentResult for unmodified artifacts. mark_modified() flags artifacts needing re-evaluation. Cache is pruned via retain_valid_cache_entries(). (see @src/pipeline/refinement/engine.rs:140)

- Rich context passing via StrategyContext: StrategyContext carries file_registry, issues, suggestions, validation_feedback, and quality_acceptance_delta. Strategies use context for prompts and quality validation. (see @src/pipeline/strategy/mod.rs:113)

- Evidence feedback loop with retry budget: Evidence strategy has iterative feedback loop that retries up to max_retries times until target_refs is met. Each iteration calls LLM to enhance content. (see @src/pipeline/strategy/evidence.rs:68)

- Session management with config validation: SessionManager handles session lifecycle with create/resume logic, config hash validation, and event persistence via EventStore (see @src/pipeline/session.rs:12)
- Arc-wrapped connection pool: Database is wrapped in Arc (SharedDatabase type alias) for safe sharing across threads, with r2d2 providing the connection pooling (see @src/storage/database.rs:14)
- Contextual error wrapping: Errors are wrapped using ClaudegenError::Storage variant with descriptive messages, using .with_context() for additional context (see @src/storage/database.rs:79)
- Panic-safe transactions: Transactions use std::panic::catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe to catch panics and convert them to errors, ensuring automatic rollback (see @src/storage/database.rs:137)
- Auto-tuning pool configuration: Pool configuration auto-calculates optimal size based on CPU cores with multiplier, clamped to min/max bounds (see @src/storage/database.rs:35)
- Embedded schema pattern: SQL schema is embedded at compile time using include_str! macro, ensuring schema is always bundled with binary (see @src/storage/database.rs:16)
- In-memory test databases: Tests use open_in_memory() for isolated, fast database tests without filesystem interaction (see @src/storage/database.rs:231)
- Nested test module organization: Test modules use nested mod blocks to organize related tests by component or feature (see @tests/generators.rs:35)
- Test fixture factory pattern: Tests use helper functions that create default/empty instances of complex types for isolation (see @tests/generators.rs:18)
- Artifact validation pattern: All generated artifacts (skills, agents, rules) have validate() methods returning issues that are filtered for errors (see @tests/generators.rs:137)
- Fixed artifact counts: Generated counts are fixed: exactly 5 skills, exactly 3 agents - these are invariants verified across multiple test runs (see @tests/generators.rs:51)

- Threshold-based strategy selection: Grouping strategy is determined by module count against configurable thresholds: None(<6), SingleLevel(6-29), TwoLevel(30-99), ThreeLevel(100+) (see @tests/hierarchical_grouping.rs:137)
- Three-tier hierarchical structure: Domain rules are generated from 3-tier hierarchy: Domain contains Groups which contain Modules (see @tests/hierarchical_grouping.rs:71)

- Defense-in-depth path validation: Path validation uses a multi-layer defense: component-level traversal check, absolute path rejection, and post-canonicalization root containment verification (see @src/utils/path.rs:41)

- Layered validation with is_*/parse_* pairs: Validation functions accept &str and parse into structured types. Pattern: is_X checks bool, parse_X returns Option<structured_data> (see @src/utils/tools.rs:68)
- Lazy static initialization for expensive resources: LazyLock for expensive regex compilation, computed once on first access (see @src/utils/patterns.rs:27)
- Result enum with semantic variants: PathResolution enum encodes all possible outcomes (Safe, TraversalAttempt, AbsolutePath, EscapesRoot) with conversion methods (see @src/utils/path.rs:9)
- Const arrays for canonical tool definitions: Tool lists defined as const arrays with version comments. Separates permission-free from permission-required tools. (see @src/utils/tools.rs:14)
- Zero-dependency utility module: Module explicitly states 'No pipeline dependencies' - pure utilities usable by both types and pipeline modules (see @src/utils/mod.rs:1)

- Validation Issue Pattern: Types implement a validate() method returning Vec<ValidationIssue> for declarative validation with distinct error codes (SKILL_NAME_TOO_LONG, SKILL_DESC_EMPTY, etc.) (see @src/types/skill.rs:225)
- Builder Pattern with with_* Methods: Structs use builder pattern with with_* methods that take mut self and return Self, enabling fluent chaining (see @src/types/skill.rs:147)

- ParseWithDefault Trait for Safe Enum Parsing: Trait ParseWithDefault provides safe parsing with logged warnings and default fallbacks for enum deserialization from strings (see @src/types/utils.rs:70)
- Three-Level Diagnostic Severity: DiagnosticLevel enum with Info/Warning/Error levels, implementing Ord for severity comparison and is_error()/is_warning() helpers (see @src/types/validation.rs:4)
- JSON Extraction Helpers: Helper functions json_string, json_bool, json_i64 etc. provide ergonomic extraction from serde_json::Value with Option/default handling (see @src/types/utils.rs:23)
- Logged Error Filtering: log_filter_error and log_filter_warn functions wrap Result, logging errors before discarding them in filter_map chains (see @src/types/utils.rs:168)

- Builder pattern with with_* methods: Builder pattern with with_* methods returning Self for fluent chaining. Used consistently across Agent, Rule, Skill, ModuleScope, DomainPolicy, etc. (see @src/types/agent.rs:260)

- Multi-issue validation pattern: Validation methods return Vec<ValidationIssue> instead of Result. Allows collecting all issues at once. Check issues.is_empty() or filter by severity. (see @src/types/agent.rs:378)

- From/Into conversion pattern: Types use From trait for conversions with Into bounds on constructors (impl Into<String>). Enables both &str and String arguments without explicit conversion. (see @src/types/agent.rs:238)

- Enum string conversion triad: Enum variants have as_str() methods returning &'static str, Display impl calling as_str(), and FromStr with default fallbacks for robustness. (see @src/types/agent.rs:77)

- Unified error type with category routing: ClaudegenError is the unified error type with thiserror derives. All modules convert to this type. LlmError has category-based routing for retry decisions. (see @src/types/error.rs:248)

- Objective vs Semantic quality separation: Quality is split into ObjectiveQuality (deterministic: reference counts, structure) and SemanticQuality (LLM-evaluated: tier, actionability). Combined in ArtifactQuality. (see @src/types/quality.rs:12)

- LLM extraction pattern: All phase modules follow extract_with_llm pattern: build prompt, generate schema, call provider.generate(), deserialize response with deserialize_llm_response() (see @src/pipeline/phases/constraint_extraction.rs:222)

- Graceful LLM fallback: When LLM calls fail, phases fall back to static analysis results with tracing::warn log, returning partial results rather than propagating errors (see @src/pipeline/phases/constraint_extraction.rs:144)

- Dual API pattern (simple + enhanced): Phases expose both simple method (e.g., extract()) and enhanced method (e.g., extract_with_synthesis()) allowing callers to provide additional context (see @src/pipeline/phases/constraint_extraction.rs:119)
- Serde default for LLM output structs: LLM output types use #[serde(default)] extensively to handle missing fields gracefully during deserialization (see @src/pipeline/phases/module_detection.rs:49)

- Static few-shot library pattern: Few-shot examples are organized as static constants (FewShotExample structs) with getter functions that dispatch based on ProjectType enum (see @src/pipeline/phases/few_shot.rs:42)
- Module re-export pattern: mod.rs re-exports key types from submodules using pub use, creating a clean public API surface (see @src/pipeline/phases/mod.rs:25)

- Validation Pipeline Pattern: ValidationPipeline combines parsing (structured_output) and validation (ResponseValidator) into a single process() call that returns both parsed value and validation results (see @src/ai/validation/mod.rs:30)
- Error Code Convention: Errors have codes (RESP001, FILE001, SEC001, etc.) with prefixes indicating category, enabling programmatic error handling (see @src/ai/validation/response.rs:68)
- Builder Pattern for Validation Results: Diagram validation structs use builder pattern with with_* methods for optional fields (see @src/ai/validation/diagram.rs:48)
- Robust LLM Output Preprocessing: JSON preprocessing pipeline: trim -> BOM removal -> code fence extraction -> JSON extraction from surrounding text (see @src/ai/validation/structured_output.rs:33)
- Tiered Validation Severity: Three-tier validation severity: errors (block), warnings (acceptable but noted), info (informational) (see @src/ai/validation/response.rs:21)
- Diagram Type Dispatch: Each diagram type (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, gantt, pie) has its own validation function with type-specific rules (see @src/ai/validation/diagram.rs:126)
- Phased Pipeline Execution: Pipeline executes numbered phases sequentially with dependencies. Each phase stores results in ClaudegenContext for downstream phases. (see @src/pipeline/adaptive.rs:130)
- Lazy Initialization with OnceCell: Uses OnceCell for lazy initialization of expensive resources that should only be computed once. (see @src/pipeline/adaptive.rs:66)

- Map-Reduce Aggregation: Chunk results are aggregated using map-reduce: individual chunks are analyzed in parallel, then reduced via AnalysisAggregator::aggregate() (see @src/pipeline/analysis/aggregator.rs:104)

- Sigmoid Saturation for Confidence Scoring: Confidence scores use 5 dimensions with sigmoid saturation. saturate(count, saturation_point) returns diminishing value approaching 1.0. (see @src/pipeline/analysis/confidence.rs:139)
- AST Ground-Truth Validation: AST enrichment extracts ground-truth facts via tree-sitter, used to validate LLM analysis and prevent hallucinations. (see @src/pipeline/analysis/ast_enrichment.rs:146)

- Type-Safe Analysis Conversion with Quality Tracking: AnalysisConverter trait provides type-safe conversion between analysis types with quality tracking and loss detection. (see @src/pipeline/analysis/converter.rs:17)

- Graceful Degradation on Analysis Failure: Graceful degradation pattern: on failure or timeout, log warning and continue with partial/default results rather than failing pipeline. (see @src/pipeline/adaptive.rs:173)

- Core+Extended Skill Layering: Two-layer skill architecture: Core skills (5 universal) generated first, Extended skills (conditional) generated based on ProjectEvidence detection (see @src/pipeline/generation/skills/mod.rs:47)
- Evidence-Tiered Prompt Building: EvidenceTier-aware prompt generation with verified references only - prevents line number hallucination (see @src/pipeline/generation/skills/prompt.rs:146)
- SkillGeneration Config Pattern: Config-driven skill generation with three modes: Auto (evidence-based), Enabled (always), Disabled (never) (see @src/pipeline/generation/skills/extended.rs:19)
- Value Tier Classification: Value-based section classification (Critical/High/Normal tiers) for progressive disclosure decisions (see @src/pipeline/generation/skills/disclosure.rs:35)
- Test Context Factory: Test context factory pattern using references to avoid ownership issues in test setup (see @src/pipeline/generation/skills/core.rs:216)

- Command Options Builder Pattern: Commands use builder pattern with options struct, then delegate to async implementation via run_async. Synchronous run() creates tokio Runtime. (see @src/cli/commands/generate.rs:30)

- Result Type with Domain Errors: All commands return crate::types::Result<T>, using ? operator for propagation. Specific error variants like ClaudegenError::Verification for validation failures. (see @src/cli/commands/validate.rs:181)

### Core Policies

- **Artifact Names Must Be Kebab-Case** (validation): All artifact names (Skills, Agents, Rules) must use kebab-case format - lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, maximum 64 characters for skills
  - Evidence: @types/:0
- **Evidence-Based Generation Only** (dataintegrity): All generated artifacts must be derived from actual codebase analysis with evidence traceability. Artifacts with no file references (reference_density < 0.1) are automatically downgraded to Tier1Generic regardless of LLM classification
  - Evidence: @types/:0
- **Line Reference Validation** (validation): Line numbers must be 1-indexed (never 0), within file bounds, and validated against actual file content. Line 0 is treated as file-level reference only. References can have 5-line variance for AST validation to account for code changes
  - Evidence: @pipeline/:0
- **Value Weights Sum Invariant** (invariant): Configuration weights for value assessment (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness) must sum to exactly 1.0 with a tolerance of 0.01
  - Evidence: @config/:0
- **Database Connection Configuration** (dataintegrity): SQLite connections must be configured with WAL mode, foreign keys ON, and specific PRAGMA settings. In-memory databases must use max_size=1 for connection pool. Pool sizing must be between MIN_POOL_SIZE (4) and MAX_POOL_SIZE (32)
  - Evidence: @storage/:0
- **Quality Retention Threshold** (businessrule): Content refinement must retain at least 85% of original quality (MIN_QUALITY_RETENTION_RATIO = 0.85) and improve quality by at least quality_acceptance_delta (default 0.02 = 2%) to be accepted
  - Evidence: @pipeline/:0
- **Role-Based Tool Permissions** (authorization): Read-only roles (reviewer, architect, plan, code-review) must not have Edit, Write, or Bash tools. Tool permissions are separated into permission-free and permission-required categories
  - Evidence: @tests/:0
- **Core Skills Count Invariant** (invariant): Core skills (code-review, implement, plan, debug, refactor) must always number exactly 5 and be generated before extended skills. Extended skills are conditional on ProjectEvidence detection
  - Evidence: @pipeline/:0
- **Tier1 Finding Rejection** (businessrule): Tier1 findings (generic/rejected) are filtered out during validation and never appear in final corpus. Tier1 ratio >= 20% triggers overall Tier1 classification regardless of other content quality
  - Evidence: @pipeline/:0
- **Static Validation Before LLM** (validation): Static validation (deterministic checks) must run before LLM calls to catch issues at zero cost. Tier0 hallucinated references must be detected before LLM evaluation
  - Evidence: @pipeline/:0
- **File Registry Initialization** (invariant): File registry must be initialized before any reference validation. Module paths must exist in file registry. Registry must be built with gitignore-aware walking using ignore crate's WalkBuilder

- **Path Security Validation** (validation): All path operations must use safe_resolve/safe_join. Multi-layer defense: component-level traversal check, absolute path rejection, and post-canonicalization root containment verification. Symlink traversal disabled by default

- **MCP Tool Naming Convention** (validation): MCP tool names must follow exact pattern mcp__<server>__<tool> with exactly two underscores separating non-empty server and tool parts

Priority must follow hierarchy: project(100) > tech(90) > framework(85) > module(80) > domain(75) > group(70). Rules must be sorted by priority descending

- **Configuration Validation** (validation): Configuration version must be explicitly set to '2.0'. Cross-field validation order matters: base configs must be validated before derived configs. Config must be validated after loading and before use

### Core Domain Logic

- **Artifact Quality Scoring**: LlmJudge evaluates artifact quality through combined static validation and LLM-based semantic assessment. Calculates overall quality from three weighted dimensions (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness) that must sum to 1.0. Separates ObjectiveQuality (deterministic) from SemanticQuality (LLM-evaluated).
  - Impact: Determines the quality and accuracy of all generated documentation artifacts through multi-dimensional scoring
- **Distributed Analysis with Chunk Aggregation**: Map-reduce pattern for codebase analysis: chunks are analyzed in parallel with semaphore-bounded concurrency, then aggregated via AnalysisAggregator. Includes chunk-level checkpointing for crash recovery and incremental state compaction.
  - Impact: Controls memory usage during analysis and enables recovery from crashes, critical for large codebase analysis
- **Convergence Detection with Oscillation Prevention**: Detects analysis oscillation using hash-based proposal history and confidence snapshot comparison. Tracks consecutive failures with bounded retries (max_failures default 2). Uses sigmoid saturation for confidence scoring across 5 dimensions.
  - Impact: Prevents infinite loops and ensures analysis converges to stable results within bounded iterations
- **Evidence Reference Validation**: Validates file references in generated content against VerifiedFileRegistry with graduated status (Valid, FileLevelOnly, DirectoryOnly, FileNotFound, LineOutOfRange). Uses 6-step path resolution strategy for various project structures.
  - Impact: Ensures documentation accuracy by validating all file references against actual codebase, preventing hallucinated line numbers
- **Semantic Constraint Routing**: Routes constraints and patterns to relevant agents/skills via GenerationContext based on semantic analysis. Converts detection signals to hints with confidence levels (definitive/high/medium) for LLM interpretation.
  - Impact: Enables smart routing of documentation requests to appropriate specialized handlers based on codebase characteristics
- **Phased Pipeline Execution**: Executes numbered phases sequentially with dependencies. Each phase stores results in ClaudegenContext for downstream phases. Manages session lifecycle with checkpoint-based crash recovery and event sourcing for audit trails.
  - Impact: Coordinates the entire documentation generation workflow ensuring correct phase ordering and data flow
- **Strategy-Based Refinement Engine**: Strategy pattern with rotator selecting refinement approaches based on history and escalation level. Tracks artifact/strategy pairs that fail repeatedly, skipping after max_failures. Success clears failure history.
  - Impact: Enables iterative improvement of documentation quality through targeted refinement strategies
- **Two-Pass Validation Pipeline**: Two-pass validation combining programmatic checks (100% reliable) with LLM semantic checks. Static validation runs first to catch deterministic issues at zero cost. Returns Vec<ValidationIssue> with three-tier severity (errors block, warnings acceptable, info informational).
  - Impact: Ensures generated documentation meets quality standards before output, reducing manual review burden
- **Tiered Finding Classification**: Classifies findings into three tiers: Tier1 (generic/rejected), Tier2 (project conventions), Tier3 (high-value hidden knowledge). Uses EvidenceTier-aware prompt generation with verified references only.
  - Impact: Separates high-value institutional knowledge from generic patterns, maximizing documentation utility
- **AST Ground-Truth Enrichment**: Extracts ground-truth facts via tree-sitter AST parsing to validate LLM analysis. Combines AST evidence with LLM semantic understanding. Falls back gracefully on parse failures with warning logs.
  - Impact: Prevents LLM hallucinations by grounding generated content in verified AST-extracted facts
- **Consensus Management with Veto Power**: Manages multi-agent consensus with veto power for critical agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts). Includes checkpointing, crash recovery, and persistence for reliable consensus achievement.
  - Impact: Achieves consensus among multiple analysis perspectives for higher-quality documentation decisions
- **Incremental Change Tracking**: DependencyGraph tracks file→module→artifact relationships using blake3 hashing for efficient change detection. Enables incremental regeneration based on actual changes.
  - Impact: Enables incremental documentation updates when codebase changes, avoiding full regeneration
- **Project Detection and Classification**: Detects project type, extracts constraints, infers conventions, and selects appropriate few-shot examples. Uses multi-strategy monorepo detection and pattern-based file detection with const arrays.
  - Impact: Adapts generation behavior to project characteristics for optimal documentation output
- **Layered Artifact Generation**: Three-layer artifact generation: Base (always), Module (conditional on detection), Hierarchy (conditional on groups/domains). Follows Core+Extended skill layering with 5 universal skills plus conditional extended skills.
  - Impact: Generates contextually appropriate documentation artifacts based on project analysis
- **Tiered Provider Routing**: Routes LLM requests to different model tiers (fast/default/performance) based on pipeline phase. Includes circuit breaker for resilience, budget tracking with lock-free atomics, and retry configuration.
  - Impact: Optimizes API costs and latency by routing requests to appropriate model tiers
- **Circuit Breaker for Provider Resilience**: Tracks consecutive failures and blocks requests when threshold exceeded. Automatically recovers after cooldown period. Integrated with provider chain for failover.
  - Impact: Prevents cascading failures when LLM providers experience issues, maintaining system stability
- **Schema-Driven Response Validation**: Transforms JSON schemas for strict structured output, adding additionalProperties:false and converting oneOf to Claude-compatible formats. Includes robust preprocessing pipeline for LLM output.
  - Impact: Ensures generated content conforms to expected schemas, reducing downstream errors
- **Quality Loop with Feedback**: Iterative refinement loop with evidence feedback. Retries up to max_retries until target_refs met. Each iteration calls LLM to enhance content. Includes selective judgment caching for unmodified artifacts.
  - Impact: Ensures artifact quality improves iteratively within budget and time constraints
- **Priority-Ordered Rule Generation**: Generates rules from 3-tier hierarchy (Domain→Groups→Modules) with priority-based ordering (100=project, 90=tech, 85=framework, 80=module, 75=domain, 70=group).
  - Impact: Generates hierarchical rules that reflect actual codebase organization and domain boundaries

### Glossary

- **Artifact**: Generated output item including Skills, Agents, and Rules that encode project knowledge
- **Skill**: Defines HOW - methodology for performing a specific task like code-review, implement, plan, debug, or refactor
- **Agent**: Defines WHO - a role that performs actions, such as reviewer, coder, or architect
- **Rule**: Defines WHAT - knowledge and constraints that govern behavior, with priority-based hierarchy
- **Core Skill**: Five universal skills always generated: code-review, implement, plan, debug, refactor
- **Extended Skill**: Conditional skills generated based on project evidence: test, document, security-audit
- **Base Agent**: Three universal agents always generated: reviewer, coder, architect
- **Module Specialist**: Agent specialized for a specific module when meeting value and coverage thresholds
- **Domain Expert**: Agent specialized for a domain area in the project
- **Corpus**: A validated collection of findings extracted from analysis
- **Finding**: A piece of knowledge extracted from codebase analysis, classified by tier
- **Tier1**: Generic knowledge rejected during validation - not project-specific
- **Tier2**: Project conventions - acceptable quality level for artifacts
- **Tier3**: High-value hidden knowledge - the most valuable findings
- **Module**: A cohesive unit of code with related functionality, detected through analysis
- **Group**: A collection of related modules organized together
- **Domain**: Top-level organization containing groups and modules
- **Evidence**: Traceable reference to source code that validates claims
- **Reference**: File and line reference pointing to specific code location
- **Pipeline**: Sequential execution of numbered phases for analysis and generation
- **Phase**: A discrete step in the pipeline with specific inputs and outputs
- **Extraction**: First pipeline layer - extracting raw findings from code chunks
- **Validation**: Second pipeline layer - validating findings against rules and evidence
- **Projection**: Third pipeline layer - transforming validated findings into final output
- **Chunk**: A segment of code analyzed independently then aggregated
- **Quality Score**: Numerical assessment of artifact quality across dimensions
- **Quality Dimension**: Aspect of quality measurement: actionability, evidence, mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness
- **Convergence**: State when quality scores stabilize within thresholds across iterations
- **Refinement**: Iterative improvement process to enhance artifact quality
- **Strategy**: Approach for improving artifacts: evidence enhancement, content revision, etc.
- **Oscillation**: Repeated proposals detected preventing infinite analysis loops
- **Circuit Breaker**: Pattern preventing cascading failures by blocking requests after threshold exceeded
- **Budget**: Allocation of tokens for LLM operations with tracking and limits
- **Token**: Unit of LLM consumption used for budget tracking
- **Session**: A resumable analysis instance with event sourcing for state reconstruction
- **Checkpoint**: Saved state for crash recovery during long-running operations
- **Consensus**: Multi-agent agreement process with veto power for critical agents
- **Veto**: Rejection power held by critical agents that blocks consensus
- **Provider**: LLM service endpoint with capability information
- **Provider Set**: Collection of providers with tiered routing (fast/default/performance)
- **Provider Tier**: Model capability tier for routing: fast, default, or performance
- **Constraint**: Constraint or pattern routed to relevant agents/skills
- **Pattern**: Recognized coding pattern extracted from analysis
- **Generation Context**: Context object carrying constraints and patterns for generation
- **Hub Module**: Module with high incoming dependency count (>= total_modules/3)
- **File Registry**: Registry of files validated to exist in the project
- **Reference Status**: Validation status for references: Valid, FileLevelOnly, DirectoryOnly, FileNotFound, LineOutOfRange
- **Progressive Disclosure**: UI technique showing critical content first, details on demand
- **Value Tier**: Classification based on content value: Critical, High, Normal tiers
- **Artifact Category**: Category determining artifact requirements: Methodology (Tier1 OK) or ProjectSpecific (Tier2+ required)
- **Methodology**: Artifact category allowing generic content - for core skills and base agents
- **Project Specific**: Artifact category requiring Tier2+ evidence - for extended skills and all rules
- **Rule Priority**: Rule ordering value: project(100), tech(90), framework(85), module(80), domain(75), group(70)
- **Evidence Tier**: Classification of evidence richness: Rich (requires @file:line), Moderate (mixed), Sparse (file-level)
- **Reference Density**: Ratio of content with valid file references
- **Evidence Floor**: Minimum reference density (0.1) below which artifacts are downgraded to Tier1
- **LLM Judgment**: LLM-based semantic quality assessment as authoritative decision maker
- **Static Validation**: Static validation checks before LLM calls to catch deterministic issues
- **Quality Acceptance Delta**: Minimum quality improvement (2%) required for refinement acceptance
- **Quality Retention Ratio**: Minimum quality retention (85%) required during content refinement
- **Event**: Append-only log entry for state reconstruction
- **Event Stream**: JSONL file containing events for a session
- **Compaction**: Reducing state size while preserving recovery capability
- **Project Size**: Project size category affecting thresholds: minimal (<10 files), small (<50), default
- **Grouping Strategy**: Module grouping based on count: None(<6), SingleLevel(6-29), TwoLevel(30-99), ThreeLevel(100+)
- **Validation Severity**: Validation severity: errors (blocking), warnings (noted), info (informational)
- **Error Code**: Structured error with code (RESP001, FILE001, SEC001) for programmatic handling
- **Graceful Degradation**: On failure, continue with partial results rather than failing entirely
- **Value Score**: Value determining module agent generation eligibility (threshold 0.7)
- **Coverage Ratio**: Module's code coverage percentage (threshold 2% for agent generation)

### Business Workflows

**Documentation Generation Pipeline**
Main documentation generation workflow that orchestrates multi-phase analysis, validation, and artifact creation to produce comprehensive project documentation from source code
1. Configuration Loading: Load and merge configuration from defaults, global, project, and environment sources
2. Project Detection: Detect project type, technologies, frameworks using multi-strategy detection with file patterns and content analysis
3. Constraint Extraction: Extract constraints, conventions, and patterns from codebase via semantic routing to relevant analyzers
4. Deep Analysis: Perform distributed chunk analysis with checkpointing, AST enrichment, and LLM-based extraction
5. Cross Synthesis: Aggregate chunk results using map-reduce pattern to produce unified analysis findings
6. Validation: Run two-pass validation: programmatic checks followed by LLM semantic validation
7. Artifact Generation: Generate layered artifacts: Core skills (5), Agents (3), Rules with priority ordering across three tiers
8. Quality Assessment: Evaluate artifacts using objective metrics and LLM-based semantic quality scoring
9. Refinement Loop: Iteratively improve artifacts using strategy rotation until convergence or budget exhaustion
10. Output: Write validated artifacts to configured output locations with appropriate formats

**Quality Refinement Loop**
Iterative quality improvement process using multiple strategies to refine generated artifacts until quality targets are met
1. Quality Assessment: Analyze current artifact quality using multi-dimensional scoring (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness)
2. Convergence Check: Check if quality has stabilized or oscillation detected via hash-based proposal history
3. Strategy Selection: StrategyRotator selects appropriate strategy based on applicable_to(), priority(), and history tracking
4. Strategy Execution: Execute selected refinement strategy (evidence enhancement, specificity, etc.) with rich context
5. Failure Tracking: Track artifact/strategy pair failures; skip pairs exceeding max_failures (default 2)
6. Selective Caching: Cache judgment results for unmodified artifacts; prune invalid cache entries

**Consensus-Based Review**
Multi-agent consensus process where specialized agents review and approve generated artifacts with veto power for critical decisions
1. Submission: Submit artifact for review to relevant specialist agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts)
2. Agent Review: Each agent evaluates artifact based on their expertise and provides assessment
3. Veto Check: Critical agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts) can veto and block approval
4. Consensus Aggregation: Aggregate non-vetoed assessments to determine overall consensus
5. Approval: Artifact passes review and proceeds to output
6. Rejection: Artifact rejected; feedback provided for refinement

**Incremental Sync Pipeline**
Incremental update process that tracks changes and regenerates only affected artifacts based on dependency relationships
1. Change Detection: Use Blake3 hashing to detect which files have changed since last run
2. Dependency Resolution: DependencyGraph traces file→module→artifact relationships to identify affected artifacts
3. Selective Regeneration: Regenerate only artifacts whose dependencies changed, skipping unchanged portions
4. State Update: Update tracking state with new file hashes and timestamps

**Checkpoint Recovery**
Crash recovery process using checkpoints and event sourcing to resume interrupted analysis from last known good state
1. Session Detection: Check for existing session via lock file with PID and timestamp
2. Lock Validation: Validate lock file PID is still running; handle stale locks
3. State Reconstruction: Replay JSONL event log to reconstruct state via event sourcing pattern
4. Config Validation: Verify config hash matches to ensure compatible state
5. Resume Processing: Continue from last successful checkpoint with restored context
6. Fresh Start: Initialize new session with ULID-based directory and fresh event stream

**Distributed Chunk Analysis**
Distributed analysis of large codebases using parallel chunk processing with progress tracking and fault tolerance
1. Chunk Partitioning: Partition codebase into chunks based on file boundaries and size limits
2. Parallel Analysis: Process chunks concurrently with semaphore-bounded parallelism using JoinSet
3. Chunk Checkpoint: Save checkpoint after each chunk completes for recovery capability
4. Progress Update: Broadcast progress events via Arc<RwLock> + broadcast channel pattern
5. Aggregation: Map-reduce aggregation of chunk results via AnalysisAggregator::aggregate()

**Validation Pipeline**
Multi-tier validation pipeline combining fast programmatic checks with slower LLM-based semantic validation
1. Static Validation: Fast deterministic checks: file references, required sections, structure validation
2. Reference Validation: Validate file:line references against VerifiedFileRegistry with graduated status
3. LLM Validation: Semantic quality evaluation using LlmJudge for actionability, evidence, specificity
4. Issue Aggregation: Collect all issues with three-tier severity: errors (block), warnings (note), info
5. Result Classification: Classify result as Pass, PassWithWarnings, or Fail with score and issues list
6. Early Rejection: Reject early if deterministic checks fail, saving LLM API costs

**Provider Circuit Breaker**
LLM provider management with circuit breaker pattern, budget tracking, and tiered routing for resilient API interactions
1. Request Routing: Route request to appropriate model tier (fast/default/performance) based on phase
2. Budget Check: Verify budget available using atomic CAS operations on SharedBudget
3. Circuit Check: Check circuit breaker state; block if consecutive failures exceed threshold
4. Provider Call: Execute LLM call with retry logic based on RetryConfig
5. Success Recording: Reset failure counter, update metrics, deduct from budget
6. Failure Recording: Increment failure counter, check if threshold reached to open circuit
7. Circuit Open: Block requests for cooldown period, return cached/fallback response
8. Budget Exhausted: Terminate request, trigger graceful degradation with partial results

**Layered Artifact Generation**
Hierarchical artifact generation following three-layer architecture with evidence-gated conditional generation
1. Core Layer Generation: Generate 5 core skills that apply universally to any project
2. Evidence Evaluation: Evaluate ProjectEvidence to determine which extended artifacts to generate
3. Module Layer Generation: Generate module specialists and extended skills based on detection signals
4. Hierarchy Layer Generation: Generate domain experts and group-level rules based on hierarchy depth
5. Priority Assignment: Assign priority ordering: project(100), tech(90), framework(85), module(80), domain(75), group(70)
6. Artifact Validation: Run validate() on all generated artifacts, filter by error severity
gotchas: **CircularDependency: pipeline/analysis/reanalysis -> pipeline/analysis/synthesis**: Circular dependency: pipeline/analysis/reanalysis ↔ pipeline/analysis/synthesis -> Break cycle by introducing abstraction or inverting dependency direction between pipeline/analysis/reanalysis and pipeline/analysis/synthesis

**Router-Analysis State Synchronization Gap**: Router caches analysis state for routing decisions but must be explicitly rebuilt when synthesis or cross_insights change. If code updates analysis state without rebuilding the router, routing decisions will be based on stale data, causing insights to be misrouted or lost. -> Create a wrapper type that couples analysis state mutations with automatic router invalidation, or use a builder pattern where router construction requires fresh analysis state as input.

**Budget CAS Exhaustion Under Concurrent LLM Calls**: Budget consumption uses CAS with retry limits. If concurrent requests exhaust MAX_CAS_RETRIES during high contention, budget updates silently fail. Combined with the extended context 1M token limit requiring API keys, OAuth users hitting the 200K limit may not get proper budget accounting. -> Implement budget reservation before LLM calls rather than post-hoc accounting. Add monitoring for CAS failure rates and alert when approaching retry limits.

**Skill Argument Injection is Implicit Template Dependency**: Skills with argument_hint require $ARGUMENTS placeholder injection via inject_arguments_section(). This is a runtime template expansion dependency not visible in the skill definition. Skills will silently execute without arguments if the injection step is skipped or fails. -> Validate at skill load time that any skill with argument_hint contains $ARGUMENTS placeholder, failing fast rather than at execution time.

**Progressive Disclosure Threshold Causes Context Bloat**: Progressive disclosure only activates for sections exceeding 50 lines (MIN_SECTION_SIZE_FOR_EXTRACTION). For documents with many sections just under this threshold, the full content is always included, potentially causing context window exhaustion when processing multiple artifacts. -> Track cumulative context size across sections, not just per-section size. Apply progressive disclosure based on total document size when aggregate exceeds context budget.

**Module Path Validation Against Stale File Registry**: Module detection filters LLM output against file registry, but if the registry is stale (files deleted/moved since last sync), valid LLM-detected modules get silently dropped. The incremental sync pipeline may not invalidate module caches when files change. -> Include file registry freshness timestamp in module validation. Trigger full resync when file registry age exceeds threshold or when filtered module count exceeds expected noise ratio.

**YAML Frontmatter Detection Collision with Markdown Rules**: YAML frontmatter validation using starts_with('---') can match markdown horizontal rules, potentially allowing malformed frontmatter to pass validation. Combined with the Tier1 Finding Rejection policy, this could allow findings to bypass security audit. -> Use proper YAML parser for frontmatter extraction that validates complete '---' delimited blocks and rejects ambiguous horizontal rule patterns.

**Transaction UnwindSafe Requirement Masks Partial Rollbacks**: Transaction closures require UnwindSafe for panic catching and rollback. If a transaction closure captures non-UnwindSafe state (RefCell, raw pointers), panics may leave the database in an inconsistent state with SQLite's WAL mode holding partial writes. -> Create transaction wrapper that only accepts closures with explicit UnwindSafe bound and logs/alerts on any caught panics before rollback.

**Quality Retention vs Improvement Delta Creates Rejection Oscillation**: Quality refinement requires both 85% retention AND 2% improvement delta. These constraints can conflict: a refinement that improves quality by 3% but only retains 80% of original content will be rejected, even though net quality increased. The loop may oscillate. -> Track refinement attempt history and detect oscillation patterns. After N rejected refinements, accept the highest absolute quality version rather than continuing the loop.

**MCP Tool Name Pattern Validation Deferred to Runtime**: MCP tool names must follow mcp__<server>__<tool> pattern exactly. Tools registered with incorrect underscore count will fail at runtime, but the validation only occurs during tool invocation, not registration. -> Validate MCP tool name format at registration time with compile-time macro or builder pattern that enforces the underscore structure.

**AST Line Variance Tolerance Insufficient After Checkpoint Recovery**: AST validation allows 5-line variance for references, but this tolerance compounds with code changes between analysis and validation phases. If Checkpoint Recovery restores an older analysis state after code edits, the 5-line tolerance may be insufficient, causing valid references to fail. -> Store source file hash alongside line references. Invalidate references when file hash changes rather than relying on line number tolerance.

**Violation**: Circular dependency: pipeline/analysis/reanalysis ↔ pipeline/analysis/synthesis (pipeline/analysis/reanalysis -> pipeline/analysis/synthesis): Break cycle by introducing abstraction or inverting dependency direction between pipeline/analysis/reanalysis and pipeline/analysis/synthesis

**Pipeline phases vs pipeline/phases ambiguity**: The pipeline has both a 'phases' module and individual phase modules (analysis, consensus, etc.). The 'phases' module likely orchestrates the individual phases, but the naming creates confusion about where to add new functionality. -> Check the phases module first to understand orchestration, then implement actual logic in the specific phase module

**AI response validation requires two-stage validation**: AI responses go through ai/response for parsing, then ai/validation for correctness, but the pipeline also has its own validation. Forgetting either layer can cause silent failures or inconsistent behavior. -> Always ensure both AI-level and pipeline-level validation are applied when processing AI responses

**Event-driven side effects in pipeline**: The events module in the pipeline suggests an event-driven architecture. Side effects or state changes may be triggered by events rather than direct function calls, making debugging non-linear. -> Trace event emissions and subscriptions when debugging unexpected behavior

**CLI commands depend on types module definitions**: CLI commands may require specific type definitions from the types module. Adding new commands without corresponding types can cause compilation errors or runtime type mismatches. -> Define types in src/types/ before implementing new CLI commands that use them

patterns.name: Selective re-export pattern

patterns.name: Tracing-based logging with CLI verbosity control

patterns.name: Artifact Reference to Path Mapping

patterns.name: Dependency Graph for Incremental Updates

| `validation` | Deterministic | Fast pre-checks, tier ratios, file existence | | `quality::LlmJudge` | Semantic | LLM-based content quality assessment |

patterns.name: File Reference Validation Pattern

patterns.name: Selective judgment caching

while retry < self.config.max_retries && current_refs < target { retry += 1; ... }

patterns.name: Auto-tuning pool configuration

patterns.name: In-memory test databases

patterns.name: Nested test module organization

patterns.usage_guidance: Group related tests in mod blocks named after the component being tested (skills, agents, rules, etc.)

let issues = skill.validate(); let errors: Vec<_> = issues.iter().filter(|i| i.is_error()).collect();

patterns.name: Fixed artifact counts

patterns.usage_guidance: Core skills (code-review, implement, plan, debug, refactor) and agents (reviewer, coder, architect) are fixed sets

patterns.name: Three-tier hierarchical structure

patterns.name: Defense-in-depth path validation

patterns.usage_guidance: Always use safe_resolve for any user-provided paths. Check is_safe() or use .ok() to get Option<PathBuf>

patterns.name: Zero-dependency utility module

patterns.name: Unified error type with category routing

locations.snippet: pub struct LlmError { pub category: ErrorCategory, ... }

patterns.name: Objective vs Semantic quality separation

pub struct SemanticQuality { pub tier: TierClassification, pub actionability: f32, pub project_specificity: f32 }

patterns.name: LLM extraction pattern

patterns.usage_guidance: Use generate_schema<T>() for schema generation and deserialize_llm_response() for parsing

tracing::warn!(error = %e, "LLM convention inference failed, using static analysis only")

patterns.name: Dual API pattern (simple + enhanced)

pub async fn extract_with_synthesis(&self, detection: &ProjectDetection, conventions: &InferredConventions, synthesis: Option<&SynthesizedAnalysis>) -> Result<ExtractedConstraints>

patterns.name: Serde default for LLM output structs

patterns.usage_guidance: Always use #[serde(default)] on LLM output struct fields to handle partial responses

pub fn with_suggestion(mut self, suggestion: impl Into<String>) -> Self
