patterns.usage_guidance: Always use claudegen::types::Result, not std::result::Result. Use ResultExt for context enrichment.

patterns.name: Selective re-export pattern
patterns.description: Public API is carefully curated in lib.rs through explicit re-exports. Internal modules are pub but specific types are selectively exposed.

locations.snippet: pub use analyzer::{parser::{Language, ParseResult, Parser, detect_language}, scanner::FileScanner}

patterns.usage_guidance: When adding new public types, add explicit re-export in lib.rs. Keep internal implementation details hidden.

patterns.name: Namespaced constants via nested modules
patterns.description: Constants are organized in nested modules (tools, llm, provider, validation, cli) for namespacing.

locations.snippet: pub mod tools { pub const DEFAULT_TOOLS: &[&str] = &["Read", "Glob", "Grep"]; }

patterns.usage_guidance: Add new constants to appropriate submodule. Create new submodule if category doesn't exist.

patterns.name: Tracing-based logging with CLI verbosity control
patterns.description: Uses tracing-subscriber with EnvFilter for configurable log levels. Supports --verbose (debug), --quiet (error), default (info).

locations.snippet: let filter = if cli.verbose { "debug" } else if cli.quiet { "error" } else { "info" };

patterns.usage_guidance: Use tracing macros (tracing::info!, tracing::debug!) not println!. Respect verbosity levels.

patterns.name: Artifact Reference to Path Mapping
patterns.description: ArtifactRef enum maps abstract artifact types to concrete file paths, providing single source of truth for output locations

locations.snippet: pub fn output_path(&self) -> String { match self { Self::ProjectRule => "rules/project.md".into(), ... } }

patterns.usage_guidance: Add new artifact types to ArtifactRef enum and implement output_path() to define their storage location

patterns.name: Dependency Graph for Incremental Updates
patterns.description: DependencyGraph tracks file→module→artifact relationships to enable incremental regeneration based on what actually changed

locations.snippet: pub struct DependencyGraph { file_to_module: HashMap<String, String>, module_to_artifacts: HashMap<String, Vec<ArtifactRef>>, ... }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use DependencyGraph.build() from manifest, then affected_by() to determine which artifacts need regeneration

patterns.name: Blake3-based Change Detection
patterns.description: FileTracker uses blake3 hashing to detect file changes efficiently without storing full content
patterns.usage_guidance: Call scan_and_track() to build baseline, then detect_changes() on subsequent runs to get added/modified/deleted files

patterns.name: Deterministic vs Semantic Validation Split
patterns.description: Validation and quality assessment are separated: validation handles deterministic checks (duplicates, file existence), while LlmJudge handles semantic quality

locations.snippet: This module ONLY validates deterministic properties: - Duplicate names (skill, agent, rule) - File reference existence
| `validation` | Deterministic | Fast pre-checks, tier ratios, file existence | | `quality::LlmJudge` | Semantic | LLM-based content quality assessment |

patterns.usage_guidance: Use validation module for fast pre-checks. Use LlmJudge for content quality decisions. Never use validation to reject semantically-valid content.

patterns.name: File Reference Validation Pattern
patterns.description: Evidence traceability validates file references in content against VerifiedFileRegistry, including optional line number bounds checking
patterns.usage_guidance: Use extract_references() to find file refs in text, then validate against registry. Line numbers are validated if registry has line count info.

patterns.name: Re-export Pattern for Module APIs
patterns.description: Module re-exports types through mod.rs for clean public API while keeping implementation in separate files

locations.snippet: pub use change_set::ChangeSet; pub use dependencies::{ArtifactRef, DependencyGraph}; pub use result::{...}; pub use tracker::FileTracker;

patterns.usage_guidance: Define types in submodules, re-export through mod.rs. Users import from the parent module.

patterns.name: Strategy pattern with rotator
patterns.description: Strategies implement RefinementStrategy trait with applicable_to(), priority(), and refine_* methods. StrategyRotator selects and tracks strategies based on history and escalation level

locations.snippet: pub trait RefinementStrategy: Send + Sync { fn name(&self) -> &str; fn applicable_to(&self, issue: &IssueKind) -> bool; fn priority(&self) -> u8 { 50 } async fn refine_skill(...) }
pub struct StrategyRotator { strategies: Vec<Arc<dyn RefinementStrategy>>, history: HashMap<(String, IssueKind), Vec<StrategyAttempt>> }

patterns.usage_guidance: Add new strategies by implementing RefinementStrategy trait and registering in StrategyRotator::create_strategy match arm

patterns.name: Failure tracking with bounded retries
patterns.description: Refinement tracks artifact/strategy pairs that fail repeatedly. After max_failures (default 2), the pair is skipped. Success clears failure history.

locations.snippet: pub fn should_skip(&self, artifact: &str, strategy: &str) -> bool { ... self.failures.get(&key).map(|r| r.count >= self.max_failures).unwrap_or(false) }
pub fn record_success(&mut self, artifact: &str, strategy: &str) { self.failures.remove(&key); }

patterns.usage_guidance: Always call record_success after successful refinement to reset failure counts

patterns.name: Selective judgment caching
patterns.description: RefinementState caches JudgmentResult for unmodified artifacts. mark_modified() flags artifacts needing re-evaluation. Cache is pruned via retain_valid_cache_entries().

locations.snippet: fn cache_judgment(&mut self, artifact_key: &str, result: JudgmentResult) { self.cached_judgments.insert(artifact_key.to_string(), result); }

patterns.usage_guidance: Call clear_modifications() at iteration start, mark_modified() when artifacts change, and retain_valid_cache_entries() to prune deleted artifacts

patterns.name: Rich context passing via StrategyContext
patterns.description: StrategyContext carries file_registry, issues, suggestions, validation_feedback, and quality_acceptance_delta. Strategies use context for prompts and quality validation.

locations.snippet: pub struct StrategyContext<'a> { pub file_registry: &'a VerifiedFileRegistry, pub issues: Vec<StrategyIssue>, pub suggestions: Vec<String>, pub validation_feedback: Option<ValidationFeedback>, pub quality_acceptance_delta: f32 }

patterns.usage_guidance: Build context with new() then chain with_issues(), with_suggestions(), with_validation_feedback() as needed

patterns.name: Evidence feedback loop with retry budget
patterns.description: Evidence strategy has iterative feedback loop that retries up to max_retries times until target_refs is met. Each iteration calls LLM to enhance content.

locations.snippet: pub async fn evidence_feedback_loop(&self, skill: &mut Skill, context: &StrategyContext<'_>) -> Result<EvidenceResult>
while retry < self.config.max_retries && current_refs < target { retry += 1; ... }

patterns.usage_guidance: Configure EvidenceFeedbackConfig.max_retries and target_refs to balance quality vs API costs

patterns.name: Session management with config validation
patterns.description: SessionManager handles session lifecycle with create/resume logic, config hash validation, and event persistence via EventStore

locations.snippet: pub struct SessionManager { event_store: Arc<EventStore>, resume_state: ResumeState, config_hash: String, is_resumed: bool }
pub async fn init(project_root: &Path, config: &Config) -> Result<Self> { ... if config_matches { return Self::resume(...) } Self::create_new(...) }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use SessionManager::init() which auto-detects resumable sessions and validates config hash matches

patterns.name: Arc-wrapped connection pool
patterns.description: Database is wrapped in Arc (SharedDatabase type alias) for safe sharing across threads, with r2d2 providing the connection pooling
patterns.usage_guidance: Use SharedDatabase when passing database across thread boundaries; the pool handles connection lifecycle

patterns.name: Contextual error wrapping
patterns.description: Errors are wrapped using ClaudegenError::Storage variant with descriptive messages, using .with_context() for additional context
patterns.usage_guidance: Always wrap rusqlite errors with ClaudegenError::Storage and add context describing the operation that failed

patterns.name: Panic-safe transactions
patterns.description: Transactions use std::panic::catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe to catch panics and convert them to errors, ensuring automatic rollback
patterns.usage_guidance: Use db.transaction(|conn| { ... }) for multi-statement operations; panics will be caught and rolled back automatically

patterns.name: Auto-tuning pool configuration
patterns.description: Pool configuration auto-calculates optimal size based on CPU cores with multiplier, clamped to min/max bounds

locations.snippet: pub fn optimal_pool_size() -> u32 { let cores = std::thread::available_parallelism()...

patterns.usage_guidance: Use PoolConfig::auto() or PoolConfig::default() for automatic sizing; override with open_with_config() only if needed

patterns.name: Embedded schema pattern
patterns.description: SQL schema is embedded at compile time using include_str! macro, ensuring schema is always bundled with binary
patterns.usage_guidance: Schema changes require recompilation; the schema.sql file must be in the same directory as database.rs

patterns.name: In-memory test databases
patterns.description: Tests use open_in_memory() for isolated, fast database tests without filesystem interaction

locations.snippet: let db = Database::open_in_memory().expect("Failed to open in-memory database");

patterns.usage_guidance: Always use open_in_memory() for unit tests; file-based databases should only be used for integration tests

patterns.name: Nested test module organization
patterns.description: Test modules use nested mod blocks to organize related tests by component or feature
patterns.usage_guidance: Group related tests in mod blocks named after the component being tested (skills, agents, rules, etc.)

patterns.name: Test fixture factory pattern
patterns.description: Tests use helper functions that create default/empty instances of complex types for isolation
patterns.usage_guidance: Create helper functions returning default instances to reduce test boilerplate and ensure consistent baseline state

patterns.name: Artifact validation pattern
patterns.description: All generated artifacts (skills, agents, rules) have validate() methods returning issues that are filtered for errors

locations.snippet: let issues = skill.validate(); let errors: Vec<_> = issues.iter().filter(|i| i.is_error()).collect();
let issues = skill.validate(); let errors: Vec<_> = issues.iter().filter(|i| i.is_error()).collect();

patterns.usage_guidance: Always call validate() on generated artifacts and filter with is_error() to check for blocking issues

patterns.name: Fixed artifact counts
patterns.description: Generated counts are fixed: exactly 5 skills, exactly 3 agents - these are invariants verified across multiple test runs
patterns.usage_guidance: Core skills (code-review, implement, plan, debug, refactor) and agents (reviewer, coder, architect) are fixed sets

patterns.name: Threshold-based strategy selection
patterns.description: Grouping strategy is determined by module count against configurable thresholds: None(<6), SingleLevel(6-29), TwoLevel(30-99), ThreeLevel(100+)
patterns.usage_guidance: Use GroupingThresholds configuration to control when hierarchical grouping kicks in based on project size

patterns.name: Three-tier hierarchical structure
patterns.description: Domain rules are generated from 3-tier hierarchy: Domain contains Groups which contain Modules
patterns.usage_guidance: Build hierarchy bottom-up: create modules first, group them, then create domains from groups

patterns.name: Defense-in-depth path validation
patterns.description: Path validation uses a multi-layer defense: component-level traversal check, absolute path rejection, and post-canonicalization root containment verification
patterns.usage_guidance: Always use safe_resolve for any user-provided paths. Check is_safe() or use .ok() to get Option<PathBuf>

patterns.name: Layered validation with is_*/parse_* pairs
patterns.description: Validation functions accept &str and parse into structured types. Pattern: is_X checks bool, parse_X returns Option<structured_data>
patterns.usage_guidance: Use is_* for quick validation, parse_* when you need the extracted components

patterns.name: Lazy static initialization for expensive resources
patterns.description: LazyLock for expensive regex compilation, computed once on first access
patterns.usage_guidance: Use LazyLock for patterns, compiled regexes, or other one-time initialization

patterns.name: Result enum with semantic variants
patterns.description: PathResolution enum encodes all possible outcomes (Safe, TraversalAttempt, AbsolutePath, EscapesRoot) with conversion methods

locations.snippet: pub enum PathResolution { Safe(PathBuf), TraversalAttempt, AbsolutePath, EscapesRoot }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use match for exhaustive handling or .ok() for quick Option conversion

patterns.name: Const arrays for canonical tool definitions
patterns.description: Tool lists defined as const arrays with version comments. Separates permission-free from permission-required tools.
patterns.usage_guidance: Check VALID_TOOLS for all tools, PERMISSION_FREE_TOOLS for subset that don't prompt user

patterns.name: Zero-dependency utility module
patterns.description: Module explicitly states 'No pipeline dependencies' - pure utilities usable by both types and pipeline modules
patterns.usage_guidance: Keep utils dependency-free to avoid circular dependencies. Pipeline can depend on utils, not vice versa

patterns.name: Validation Issue Pattern
patterns.description: Types implement a validate() method returning Vec<ValidationIssue> for declarative validation with distinct error codes (SKILL_NAME_TOO_LONG, SKILL_DESC_EMPTY, etc.)

locations.snippet: pub struct ValidationIssue { pub severity: DiagnosticLevel, pub code: String, pub message: String }

patterns.usage_guidance: Always use structured ValidationIssue with unique codes. Use error() for blocking issues, warning() for advisory issues.

patterns.name: Builder Pattern with with_* Methods
patterns.description: Structs use builder pattern with with_* methods that take mut self and return Self, enabling fluent chaining

locations.snippet: pub fn with_version(mut self, version: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.version = version.into(); self }
pub fn with_tools(mut self, tools: Vec<String>) -> Self

patterns.usage_guidance: Use impl Into<String> for string parameters to accept both String and &str. Always return Self for chaining.

patterns.name: ParseWithDefault Trait for Safe Enum Parsing
patterns.description: Trait ParseWithDefault provides safe parsing with logged warnings and default fallbacks for enum deserialization from strings

locations.snippet: pub trait ParseWithDefault: Sized { fn type_name() -> &'static str; fn default_value() -> Self; fn try_parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self>; }

patterns.usage_guidance: Implement for enums that need to be parsed from database/config strings. Always provide meaningful type_name() for log messages.

patterns.name: Three-Level Diagnostic Severity
patterns.description: DiagnosticLevel enum with Info/Warning/Error levels, implementing Ord for severity comparison and is_error()/is_warning() helpers

locations.snippet: pub enum DiagnosticLevel { Info, Warning, Error }
pub fn is_error(&self) -> bool { matches!(self, DiagnosticLevel::Error) }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use Error for blocking issues, Warning for advisory, Info for informational. ValidationResult::is_valid() only checks for absence of errors.

patterns.name: JSON Extraction Helpers
patterns.description: Helper functions json_string, json_bool, json_i64 etc. provide ergonomic extraction from serde_json::Value with Option/default handling
patterns.usage_guidance: Use json_string_or() when you have a sensible default. Use json_string_array() for arrays that should default to empty Vec.

patterns.name: Logged Error Filtering
patterns.description: log_filter_error and log_filter_warn functions wrap Result, logging errors before discarding them in filter_map chains

locations.snippet: pub fn log_filter_error<T, E: Display>(result: Result<T, E>, context: &str) -> Option<T>

patterns.usage_guidance: Use instead of .filter_map(|r| r.ok()) when you want visibility into discarded errors. Use warn level for important operations.

patterns.name: Builder pattern with with_* methods
patterns.description: Builder pattern with with_* methods returning Self for fluent chaining. Used consistently across Agent, Rule, Skill, ModuleScope, DomainPolicy, etc.

locations.snippet: pub fn with_color(mut self, color: AgentColor) -> Self { self.color = Some(color); self }
pub fn with_tier(mut self, tier: TierClassification) -> Self { self.tier = tier; self }
pub fn with_enforcement(mut self, level: EnforcementLevel) -> Self { self.enforcement = level; self }

patterns.usage_guidance: All domain types use this pattern. Chain with_* methods for configuration, call new() or category-specific constructors first.

patterns.name: Multi-issue validation pattern
patterns.description: Validation methods return Vec<ValidationIssue> instead of Result. Allows collecting all issues at once. Check issues.is_empty() or filter by severity.
patterns.usage_guidance: Always call validate() before persisting artifacts. Issues have error/warning severity - errors block, warnings are advisory.

patterns.name: From/Into conversion pattern
patterns.description: Types use From trait for conversions with Into bounds on constructors (impl Into<String>). Enables both &str and String arguments without explicit conversion.

locations.snippet: pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, description: impl Into<String>, prompt: impl Into<String>) -> Self
pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, content: Vec<String>) -> Self

patterns.usage_guidance: Use impl Into<String> for constructor string parameters. Callers can pass &str or String.

patterns.name: Enum string conversion triad
patterns.description: Enum variants have as_str() methods returning &'static str, Display impl calling as_str(), and FromStr with default fallbacks for robustness.

locations.snippet: fn from_str(s: &str) -> std::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> { Ok(match s.to_lowercase().as_str() { ... _ => Self::Blue }) }
pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str { match self { Self::Skill => "skill", ... } }
pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str { match self { Self::Validation => "validation", ... } }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use as_str() for serialization keys, Display for user-facing output, FromStr for parsing with graceful defaults.

patterns.name: Unified error type with category routing
patterns.description: ClaudegenError is the unified error type with thiserror derives. All modules convert to this type. LlmError has category-based routing for retry decisions.

locations.snippet: pub struct LlmError { pub category: ErrorCategory, ... }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use ClaudegenError for all error returns. Check LlmError.category for retry vs fallback decisions. Never panic - all errors recoverable.

patterns.name: Objective vs Semantic quality separation
patterns.description: Quality is split into ObjectiveQuality (deterministic: reference counts, structure) and SemanticQuality (LLM-evaluated: tier, actionability). Combined in ArtifactQuality.

locations.snippet: pub struct ObjectiveQuality { pub reference_validity: f32, pub reference_density: f32, pub structure_score: f32 }
pub struct SemanticQuality { pub tier: TierClassification, pub actionability: f32, pub project_specificity: f32 }

patterns.usage_guidance: Objective metrics can be calculated without LLM. Semantic requires LLM judgment. Use from_judgment() to construct from LLM output.

patterns.name: LLM extraction pattern
patterns.description: All phase modules follow extract_with_llm pattern: build prompt, generate schema, call provider.generate(), deserialize response with deserialize_llm_response()
patterns.usage_guidance: Use generate_schema<T>() for schema generation and deserialize_llm_response() for parsing

patterns.name: Graceful LLM fallback
patterns.description: When LLM calls fail, phases fall back to static analysis results with tracing::warn log, returning partial results rather than propagating errors

locations.snippet: tracing::warn!(error = %e, has_synthesis = synthesis.is_some(), "LLM constraint extraction failed")
tracing::warn!(error = %e, "LLM convention inference failed, using static analysis only")

patterns.usage_guidance: Always handle LLM errors gracefully with fallback to available data

patterns.name: Dual API pattern (simple + enhanced)
patterns.description: Phases expose both simple method (e.g., extract()) and enhanced method (e.g., extract_with_synthesis()) allowing callers to provide additional context

locations.snippet: pub async fn extract(&self, detection: &ProjectDetection, conventions: &InferredConventions) -> Result<ExtractedConstraints>
pub async fn extract_with_synthesis(&self, detection: &ProjectDetection, conventions: &InferredConventions, synthesis: Option<&SynthesizedAnalysis>) -> Result<ExtractedConstraints>

patterns.usage_guidance: Provide both simple and enhanced methods for backward compatibility

patterns.name: Serde default for LLM output structs
patterns.description: LLM output types use #[serde(default)] extensively to handle missing fields gracefully during deserialization
patterns.usage_guidance: Always use #[serde(default)] on LLM output struct fields to handle partial responses

patterns.name: Static few-shot library pattern
patterns.description: Few-shot examples are organized as static constants (FewShotExample structs) with getter functions that dispatch based on ProjectType enum
patterns.usage_guidance: Add new project type examples as static constants and update getter match arms

patterns.name: Module re-export pattern
patterns.description: mod.rs re-exports key types from submodules using pub use, creating a clean public API surface

locations.snippet: pub use constraint_extraction::{AntiPattern, ComplexWorkflow, ExtractedConstraints, Gotcha, HiddenDependency};

patterns.usage_guidance: Re-export public types in mod.rs for cleaner imports by consumers

patterns.name: Validation Pipeline Pattern
patterns.description: ValidationPipeline combines parsing (structured_output) and validation (ResponseValidator) into a single process() call that returns both parsed value and validation results
patterns.usage_guidance: Use ValidationPipeline.process() for full parsing+validation, or validate_only() if you already have parsed JSON

patterns.name: Error Code Convention
patterns.description: Errors have codes (RESP001, FILE001, SEC001, etc.) with prefixes indicating category, enabling programmatic error handling
patterns.usage_guidance: Use prefix RESP for response-level, FILE for file-level, SEC for section-level, COV for coverage, META for metadata errors

patterns.name: Builder Pattern for Validation Results
patterns.description: Diagram validation structs use builder pattern with with_* methods for optional fields

locations.snippet: pub fn with_warnings(mut self, warnings: Vec<DiagramWarning>) -> Self
pub fn with_suggestion(mut self, suggestion: impl Into<String>) -> Self

patterns.usage_guidance: Chain with_* methods for optional data: DiagramError::new(line, msg).with_suggestion(hint)

patterns.name: Robust LLM Output Preprocessing
patterns.description: JSON preprocessing pipeline: trim -> BOM removal -> code fence extraction -> JSON extraction from surrounding text
patterns.usage_guidance: Always use parse_structured_output() for LLM responses - it handles code fences, BOM, and text wrapping

patterns.name: Tiered Validation Severity
patterns.description: Three-tier validation severity: errors (block), warnings (acceptable but noted), info (informational)
patterns.usage_guidance: Use is_valid() to check for blocking errors, warning_count() for non-blocking issues

patterns.name: Diagram Type Dispatch
patterns.description: Each diagram type (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, gantt, pie) has its own validation function with type-specific rules
patterns.usage_guidance: When adding new diagram types, add to detect_diagram_type() and create validate_<type>() method

patterns.name: Phased Pipeline Execution
patterns.description: Pipeline executes numbered phases sequentially with dependencies. Each phase stores results in ClaudegenContext for downstream phases.
patterns.usage_guidance: Add new phases with incremental numbers, store results in ctx.set_*(), access previous phase results from ctx

patterns.name: Lazy Initialization with OnceCell
patterns.description: Uses OnceCell for lazy initialization of expensive resources that should only be computed once.
patterns.usage_guidance: Use OnceCell for expensive resources needed multiple times. Call get_or_try_init() for async initialization.

patterns.name: Map-Reduce Aggregation
patterns.description: Chunk results are aggregated using map-reduce: individual chunks are analyzed in parallel, then reduced via AnalysisAggregator::aggregate()
patterns.usage_guidance: Add new aggregation dimensions by implementing reduce_X methods following the voting/counting pattern

patterns.name: Sigmoid Saturation for Confidence Scoring
patterns.description: Confidence scores use 5 dimensions with sigmoid saturation. saturate(count, saturation_point) returns diminishing value approaching 1.0.

locations.snippet: pub fn saturate(count: usize, saturation_point: usize) -> f32

patterns.usage_guidance: At saturation_point, result ~0.73. At 2x, ~0.88. At 3x, ~0.95. Use for diminishing returns on quantity metrics.

patterns.name: AST Ground-Truth Validation
patterns.description: AST enrichment extracts ground-truth facts via tree-sitter, used to validate LLM analysis and prevent hallucinations.

locations.snippet: pub async fn extract_facts(project_root: &Path, files: impl Iterator<Item = &String>) -> AstFacts
pub fn validate_function_reference(&self, name: &str, file: &str, line: u32) -> AstValidation

patterns.usage_guidance: Use AstValidator::validate_reference() to check @file:line references. Returns Exact, Close, WrongLine, WrongFile, or NotFound.

patterns.name: Type-Safe Analysis Conversion with Quality Tracking
patterns.description: AnalysisConverter trait provides type-safe conversion between analysis types with quality tracking and loss detection.

locations.snippet: pub trait AnalysisConverter { type Source; type Target; fn convert(...) -> ConversionResult<Self::Target>; }

patterns.usage_guidance: Implement AnalysisConverter for new conversion paths. Check ConversionQuality.overall_quality() and warnings for conversion issues.

patterns.name: Graceful Degradation on Analysis Failure
patterns.description: Graceful degradation pattern: on failure or timeout, log warning and continue with partial/default results rather than failing pipeline.
patterns.usage_guidance: Wrap optional analysis phases with match on Result, log warnings on failure, continue with None/default values

patterns.name: Core+Extended Skill Layering
patterns.description: Two-layer skill architecture: Core skills (5 universal) generated first, Extended skills (conditional) generated based on ProjectEvidence detection
patterns.usage_guidance: Always generate core skills first; extended skills depend on evidence detection from extract_evidence()

patterns.name: Evidence-Tiered Prompt Building
patterns.description: EvidenceTier-aware prompt generation with verified references only - prevents line number hallucination
patterns.usage_guidance: Pass verified_refs to SkillPromptBuilder; use file-level refs when line numbers unverified

patterns.name: SkillGeneration Config Pattern
patterns.description: Config-driven skill generation with three modes: Auto (evidence-based), Enabled (always), Disabled (never)
patterns.usage_guidance: Use SkillGeneration::Auto for evidence-based decisions; Enabled/Disabled for explicit overrides

patterns.name: Value Tier Classification
patterns.description: Value-based section classification (Critical/High/Normal tiers) for progressive disclosure decisions
patterns.usage_guidance: Tier3 (Critical) sections always stay in main SKILL.md; Tier1 (Normal) can be extracted if substantial

patterns.name: Test Context Factory
patterns.description: Test context factory pattern using references to avoid ownership issues in test setup
patterns.usage_guidance: Create owned data first, then pass references to test_context() for GenerationContext construction

patterns.name: Command Options Builder Pattern
patterns.description: Commands use builder pattern with options struct, then delegate to async implementation via run_async. Synchronous run() creates tokio Runtime.

locations.snippet: pub fn run(options: GenerateOptions) -> Result<()> { let rt = Runtime::new()?; rt.block_on(run_async(options)) }

patterns.usage_guidance: Create XxxOptions struct with Default derive, add builder-style with_xxx methods on the pipeline/loop, call run() which creates runtime and delegates to run_async()

patterns.name: Result Type with Domain Errors
patterns.description: All commands return crate::types::Result<T>, using ? operator for propagation. Specific error variants like ClaudegenError::Verification for validation failures.

locations.snippet: return Err(ClaudegenError::Config("Already initialized. Use --force to overwrite.".to_string()))

patterns.usage_guidance: Use crate::types::Result everywhere. Create specific ClaudegenError variants for distinguishable failure modes.

patterns.name: ConfigLoader for Merged Configuration
patterns.description: Commands that need config call ConfigLoader::load_for_project(&project_root, config_path) to get merged global+project config
patterns.usage_guidance: Always use ConfigLoader::load_for_project() rather than loading config files directly. Handles global/project merge and defaults.

patterns.name: Arc<RwLock> + Broadcast for Progress Tracking
patterns.description: ProgressTracker uses broadcast channel for events, Arc<RwLock> for shared state, AtomicBool/AtomicU64 for counters. Clone shares all state.

locations.snippet: sender: broadcast::Sender<ProgressEvent>, state: Arc<RwLock<ProgressState>>, active: Arc<AtomicBool>

patterns.usage_guidance: Subscribe to events via tracker.subscribe(). State is always consistent via lock helpers that handle poisoning.

patterns.name: Frontmatter Parsing for Artifacts
patterns.description: YAML frontmatter parsing extracts structured metadata from markdown files. Returns (Mapping, body_string) tuple.
patterns.usage_guidance: Check for --- delimiter, extract YAML between delimiters, parse with serde_yaml. Return None if no frontmatter found.

patterns.name: Multi-strategy Monorepo Detection
patterns.description: Monorepo detection checks for workspace config files (pnpm-workspace.yaml, turbo.json, etc.) and content patterns ([workspace] in Cargo.toml)
patterns.usage_guidance: Aligned with project_detection.rs detect_workspace(). Check file existence first, then content patterns for files that need inspection.

patterns.name: Styled Console Output Helper
patterns.description: Output struct wraps console crate for styled terminal output with semantic methods (success, error, warning, info, header, section)

locations.snippet: pub struct Output; impl Output { pub fn success(&self, message: &str) { println!("{} {}", style("✓").green(), message); } }

patterns.usage_guidance: Use Output struct for user-facing messages. Keep println! for structured data output (JSON mode).

constraints.title: Process lock must be acquired before session operations
constraints.description: Lock files use PID-based locking mechanism that must be checked before accessing session resources
constraints.rationale: Concurrent access prevention requires checking lock ownership before modifying session state

evidence.context: Lock file contains PID, timestamp, and hostname for process identification

constraints.title: Configuration version compatibility requirement
constraints.description: Configuration version must be explicitly set to '2.0' for compatibility with current claudegen features

evidence.context: if (fact.line as i32 - line as i32).abs() <= 5 { return AstValidation::Close { actual_line: fact.line }; }

constraints.title: Hub module threshold calculation
constraints.description: Hub modules are identified when incoming edges >= max(total_modules/3, 2). This threshold prevents small projects from flagging every module.
constraints.rationale: Identifies central architectural components for LLM consumption without over-flagging in small codebases

evidence.context: let hub_threshold = (modules.len() / 3).max(2); // Hub threshold: modules with incoming edges >= 1/3 of total modules (min 2)

constraints.title: ProjectCommands derivation pattern
constraints.description: ProjectCommands must only be derived through from_detection() using language and manifest patterns - never hardcoded per-project
constraints.rationale: Command detection relies on pattern matching against language/manifest combinations to ensure consistent behavior across projects

constraints.title: Core skills count invariant
constraints.description: Core skills must always number exactly 5 (code-review, implement, plan, debug, refactor) and be generated before extended skills
constraints.rationale: Core skills are universal methodologies; extended skills are conditional. Order matters for consistent skill indexing

constraints.title: $ARGUMENTS placeholder injection required
constraints.description: Skills with argument_hint must have $ARGUMENTS placeholder injected into body via inject_arguments_section()
constraints.rationale: $ARGUMENTS placeholder enables Claude to receive user input; missing placeholder breaks skill invocation

constraints.title: Tier3 constraints priority ordering
constraints.description: Tier3 constraints must always be routed first with highest priority, before regular constraints
constraints.rationale: Tier3 insights represent critical hidden constraints discovered through deep analysis - they must never be deprioritized

constraints.title: Progressive disclosure value preservation
constraints.description: Progressive disclosure only applies when sections exceed MIN_SECTION_SIZE_FOR_EXTRACTION (50 lines) - never truncate high-value content
constraints.rationale: High-quality content must never be removed; disclosure is for organization, not truncation

constraints.title: Line reference validation (1-indexed, within bounds)
constraints.description: PostGenerationValidator must reject line 0 references (1-indexed) and lines exceeding file length
constraints.rationale: Line number hallucination is a P0 issue; validation prevents invalid @file:line references from reaching output

evidence.context: Some(max) if r.line > max => RefStatus::LineOutOfRange { max }

constraints.title: Project must be initialized before most operations
constraints.description: The .claudegen directory must exist before running most commands except init
constraints.rationale: Commands that depend on project state check is_initialized() first and fail fast with helpful error messages

constraints.title: Validation failures must return specific error type
constraints.description: Validation errors should use ClaudegenError::Verification, not panic or generic errors
constraints.rationale: Allows callers to distinguish validation failures from other error types for appropriate handling

constraints.title: Artifact files require YAML frontmatter
constraints.description: Skills and agents must have YAML frontmatter; files without frontmatter are logged as warnings and skipped
constraints.rationale: Structured frontmatter enables consistent parsing of artifact metadata and validation

constraints.title: Budget and metrics must be attached to QualityLoop
constraints.description: QualityLoop must have budget and metrics attached for proper token tracking; use with_budget() and with_metrics() builder methods
constraints.rationale: Without budget tracking, generation could exceed token limits without warning

policies.name: Artifact Names Must Be Kebab-Case
policies.description: All artifact names (Skills, Agents, Rules) must use kebab-case format - lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, maximum 64 characters for skills

policies.name: Evidence-Based Generation Only
policies.description: All generated artifacts must be derived from actual codebase analysis with evidence traceability. Artifacts with no file references (reference_density < 0.1) are automatically downgraded to Tier1Generic regardless of LLM classification

policies.name: Line Reference Validation
policies.description: Line numbers must be 1-indexed (never 0), within file bounds, and validated against actual file content. Line 0 is treated as file-level reference only. References can have 5-line variance for AST validation to account for code changes

policies.name: Value Weights Sum Invariant
policies.description: Configuration weights for value assessment (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness) must sum to exactly 1.0 with a tolerance of 0.01

policies.name: Database Connection Configuration
policies.description: SQLite connections must be configured with WAL mode, foreign keys ON, and specific PRAGMA settings. In-memory databases must use max_size=1 for connection pool. Pool sizing must be between MIN_POOL_SIZE (4) and MAX_POOL_SIZE (32)

policies.name: Quality Retention Threshold
policies.description: Content refinement must retain at least 85% of original quality (MIN_QUALITY_RETENTION_RATIO = 0.85) and improve quality by at least quality_acceptance_delta (default 0.02 = 2%) to be accepted

policies.name: Role-Based Tool Permissions
policies.description: Read-only roles (reviewer, architect, plan, code-review) must not have Edit, Write, or Bash tools. Tool permissions are separated into permission-free and permission-required categories

policies.name: Core Skills Count Invariant
policies.description: Core skills (code-review, implement, plan, debug, refactor) must always number exactly 5 and be generated before extended skills. Extended skills are conditional on ProjectEvidence detection

policies.name: Tier1 Finding Rejection
policies.description: Tier1 findings (generic/rejected) are filtered out during validation and never appear in final corpus. Tier1 ratio >= 20% triggers overall Tier1 classification regardless of other content quality

policies.name: Static Validation Before LLM
policies.description: Static validation (deterministic checks) must run before LLM calls to catch issues at zero cost. Tier0 hallucinated references must be detected before LLM evaluation

policies.name: File Registry Initialization
policies.description: File registry must be initialized before any reference validation. Module paths must exist in file registry. Registry must be built with gitignore-aware walking using ignore crate's WalkBuilder

policies.name: Path Security Validation
policies.description: All path operations must use safe_resolve/safe_join. Multi-layer defense: component-level traversal check, absolute path rejection, and post-canonicalization root containment verification. Symlink traversal disabled by default

policies.name: MCP Tool Naming Convention
policies.description: MCP tool names must follow exact pattern mcp__<server>__<tool> with exactly two underscores separating non-empty server and tool parts

policies.name: Rule Category and Priority
policies.description: Rules are ALWAYS ProjectSpecific category requiring Tier2+ content and minimum evidence references. Priority must follow hierarchy: project(100) > tech(90) > framework(85) > module(80) > domain(75) > group(70). Rules must be sorted by priority descending

policies.name: Transaction Panic Safety
policies.description: Transaction closures must implement UnwindSafe. Transactions use std::panic::catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe to catch panics and convert them to errors, ensuring automatic rollback

policies.name: Circuit Breaker Consistency
policies.description: Circuit breakers track consecutive failures and block requests when threshold exceeded. They are shared via Arc across ProviderChain clones to maintain consistent failure tracking

policies.name: Bounded Collection Limits
policies.description: All collections in consensus types and RefinementState must be bounded with explicit MAX_* constants. FailureTracker prunes at MAX_TRACKED_PAIRS (5000), iteration progress at MAX_ITERATION_PROGRESS (5)

policies.name: Oscillation Detection Required
policies.description: ProposalHistory must check for oscillation (repeated proposals) to detect consensus deadlocks. Oscillation detection must halt reanalysis to prevent infinite analysis loops

policies.name: Configuration Validation
policies.description: Configuration version must be explicitly set to '2.0'. Cross-field validation order matters: base configs must be validated before derived configs. Config must be validated after loading and before use

policies.name: Project Initialization Required
policies.description: The .claudegen directory must exist before running most commands except init. Skills and agents must have YAML frontmatter. Files without frontmatter are logged as warnings and skipped

policies.name: Token Budget Management
policies.description: Extended context (1M tokens) requires API key authentication; OAuth mode limited to 200K context. Budget consumption uses compare-and-swap with MAX_CAS_RETRIES. Budget and metrics must be attached to QualityLoop

policies.name: Artifact Content Requirements
policies.description: Skills must have non-empty description and body content with minimum 100 characters for body and 200 characters for agent prompts. Skills with argument_hint must have $ARGUMENTS placeholder injected

policies.name: Confidence Score Bounds
policies.description: Confidence values must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive. Analysis synthesis must meet configurable min_confidence threshold. HYBRID_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD (0.7), CONFIDENCE_NORMALIZATION_DIVISOR (2.0) are empirical values

policies.name: Module Agent Generation Thresholds
policies.description: Module specialist agents only generated when value_score >= 0.7 and coverage_ratio >= 2%. Module detection converts LLM output to validated modules, filtering out modules with no verified paths

policies.name: Atomic Checkpoint Writes
policies.description: Checkpoint files must be written atomically using temp file + rename pattern. Lock files use PID-based locking mechanism that must be checked before accessing session resources

policies.name: Agent Context Fork Requirement
policies.description: When using agent field in a Skill, context must be set to 'fork'. Using agent without fork context generates a validation warning

policies.name: Language Detection Single Source
policies.description: Language detection must use the canonical Language enum from language.rs based ONLY on file extensions, NOT manifest files. No duplicate implementations permitted

policies.name: Build Directory Exclusion
policies.description: Specific directories must always be excluded from file scanning: target, node_modules, vendor, .git, dist, build, __pycache__, etc.

policies.name: Evidence Coverage Threshold
policies.description: Evidence coverage must be at least 50% (EVIDENCE_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD) for cross-validation to pass. All anti-patterns, hidden_dependencies, and implicit_rules must have file:line evidence entries

policies.name: Strategy Rotator Non-Empty
policies.description: StrategyRotator must always have at least one strategy - construction enforces this invariant with warning log and default strategy addition if empty. Strategy history preserved during escalation

policies.name: Convergence Path Priority
policies.description: Quality assessment has multiple convergence paths with strict priority ordering: EarlyExit > QualityFloorMet > QualityTargetMet > others. Quality dimensions have tiered requirements

policies.name: Graceful LLM Fallback
policies.description: When LLM extraction fails, fall back to synthesis-only constraints or static analysis results with tracing::warn log. Return partial results rather than propagating errors

policies.name: Corpus Stats Consistency
policies.description: ValidatedCorpus must call update_stats() after any modification to findings. Reference enforcement must remove non-existent file references and correct invalid line numbers

policies.name: Router Rebuild on State Change
policies.description: Router must be rebuilt when synthesis or cross_insights are updated. Tier3 constraints must always be routed first with highest priority

policies.name: ProjectCommands Derivation
policies.description: ProjectCommands must only be derived through from_detection() using language and manifest patterns - never hardcoded per-project

policies.name: ProjectRule Structural Regeneration
policies.description: When files are added or deleted (not just modified), the ProjectRule must always be regenerated to reflect structural changes

policies.name: Error Exit Code Standardization
policies.description: Exit codes must be standardized through ErrorCategory system using e.exit_code(). Validation errors should use ClaudegenError::Verification, not panic or generic errors

policies.name: Config Loading Isolation
policies.description: When loading config for a different project than CWD, never fall back to CWD's project config. Use load_for_project() which calls load_global_only() when target has no config

policies.name: Evidence Tier Prompt Selection
policies.description: Evidence tier must be checked before generation to select appropriate prompt variant - Rich tier requires @file:line, Moderate allows mix, Sparse uses file-level only

policies.name: Progressive Disclosure Value Preservation
policies.description: Progressive disclosure only applies when sections exceed MIN_SECTION_SIZE_FOR_EXTRACTION (50 lines) - never truncate high-value content

policies.name: Diagram Validation Strictness
policies.description: Validation follows fail-loudly philosophy - invalid diagrams should return errors, not silent failures. Complexity must be one of: low, medium, high, critical

policies.name: Parser Trait Implementation
policies.description: All parsers must implement the Parser trait. Parser construction should validate tree-sitter language availability at construction time, not at parse time

policies.name: State Compaction Required
policies.description: IncrementalCompactor must be run periodically to prevent unbounded state growth in quality_history, level_history, and strategy_outcomes

policies.name: Merge Provenance Tracking
policies.description: Merge strategies must track provenance and generate conflict logs for auditability. FindingId and ConflictId use ULID for uniqueness

policies.name: Tier Ratio Advisory Only
policies.description: Tier distribution checking is informational only - never reject content based on tier ratios. LlmJudge makes final quality decisions. Tier classification is advisory-only in validation

policies.name: Claims Require Evidence Lines
policies.description: All section claims in LLM responses must include evidence_lines citing source line numbers for traceability

policies.name: OpenAI Schema Wrapping
policies.description: OpenAI API requires array schemas to be wrapped in object with 'items' property due to strict mode limitations. Schema transformation adds additionalProperties:false

policies.name: LLM Retry with Exponential Backoff
policies.description: LLM calls use exponential backoff retry (1s, 2s, 4s) for rate limits and transient errors - max 3 retries. Evidence strategy has iterative feedback loop up to max_retries

policies.name: CI Workflow Requirements
policies.description: Tests must use Rust nightly toolchain exclusively. All jobs use Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with cache-on-failure: true. Security audit only runs on push events, not PRs

core_logic.name: Artifact Quality Scoring
core_logic.description: LlmJudge evaluates artifact quality through combined static validation and LLM-based semantic assessment. Calculates overall quality from three weighted dimensions (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness) that must sum to 1.0. Separates ObjectiveQuality (deterministic) from SemanticQuality (LLM-evaluated).
core_logic.business_impact: Determines the quality and accuracy of all generated documentation artifacts through multi-dimensional scoring

core_logic.name: Distributed Analysis with Chunk Aggregation
core_logic.description: Map-reduce pattern for codebase analysis: chunks are analyzed in parallel with semaphore-bounded concurrency, then aggregated via AnalysisAggregator. Includes chunk-level checkpointing for crash recovery and incremental state compaction.
core_logic.business_impact: Controls memory usage during analysis and enables recovery from crashes, critical for large codebase analysis

core_logic.name: Convergence Detection with Oscillation Prevention
core_logic.description: Detects analysis oscillation using hash-based proposal history and confidence snapshot comparison. Tracks consecutive failures with bounded retries (max_failures default 2). Uses sigmoid saturation for confidence scoring across 5 dimensions.
core_logic.business_impact: Prevents infinite loops and ensures analysis converges to stable results within bounded iterations

core_logic.name: Evidence Reference Validation
core_logic.description: Validates file references in generated content against VerifiedFileRegistry with graduated status (Valid, FileLevelOnly, DirectoryOnly, FileNotFound, LineOutOfRange). Uses 6-step path resolution strategy for various project structures.
core_logic.business_impact: Ensures documentation accuracy by validating all file references against actual codebase, preventing hallucinated line numbers

core_logic.name: Semantic Constraint Routing
core_logic.description: Routes constraints and patterns to relevant agents/skills via GenerationContext based on semantic analysis. Converts detection signals to hints with confidence levels (definitive/high/medium) for LLM interpretation.
core_logic.business_impact: Enables smart routing of documentation requests to appropriate specialized handlers based on codebase characteristics

core_logic.name: Phased Pipeline Execution
core_logic.description: Executes numbered phases sequentially with dependencies. Each phase stores results in ClaudegenContext for downstream phases. Manages session lifecycle with checkpoint-based crash recovery and event sourcing for audit trails.
core_logic.business_impact: Coordinates the entire documentation generation workflow ensuring correct phase ordering and data flow

core_logic.name: Strategy-Based Refinement Engine
core_logic.description: Strategy pattern with rotator selecting refinement approaches based on history and escalation level. Tracks artifact/strategy pairs that fail repeatedly, skipping after max_failures. Success clears failure history.
core_logic.business_impact: Enables iterative improvement of documentation quality through targeted refinement strategies

core_logic.name: Two-Pass Validation Pipeline
core_logic.description: Two-pass validation combining programmatic checks (100% reliable) with LLM semantic checks. Static validation runs first to catch deterministic issues at zero cost. Returns Vec<ValidationIssue> with three-tier severity (errors block, warnings acceptable, info informational).
core_logic.business_impact: Ensures generated documentation meets quality standards before output, reducing manual review burden

core_logic.name: Tiered Finding Classification
core_logic.description: Classifies findings into three tiers: Tier1 (generic/rejected), Tier2 (project conventions), Tier3 (high-value hidden knowledge). Uses EvidenceTier-aware prompt generation with verified references only.
core_logic.business_impact: Separates high-value institutional knowledge from generic patterns, maximizing documentation utility

core_logic.name: AST Ground-Truth Enrichment
core_logic.description: Extracts ground-truth facts via tree-sitter AST parsing to validate LLM analysis. Combines AST evidence with LLM semantic understanding. Falls back gracefully on parse failures with warning logs.
core_logic.business_impact: Prevents LLM hallucinations by grounding generated content in verified AST-extracted facts

core_logic.name: Consensus Management with Veto Power
core_logic.description: Manages multi-agent consensus with veto power for critical agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts). Includes checkpointing, crash recovery, and persistence for reliable consensus achievement.
core_logic.business_impact: Achieves consensus among multiple analysis perspectives for higher-quality documentation decisions

core_logic.name: Incremental Change Tracking
core_logic.description: DependencyGraph tracks file→module→artifact relationships using blake3 hashing for efficient change detection. Enables incremental regeneration based on actual changes.
core_logic.business_impact: Enables incremental documentation updates when codebase changes, avoiding full regeneration

core_logic.name: Project Detection and Classification
core_logic.description: Detects project type, extracts constraints, infers conventions, and selects appropriate few-shot examples. Uses multi-strategy monorepo detection and pattern-based file detection with const arrays.
core_logic.business_impact: Adapts generation behavior to project characteristics for optimal documentation output

core_logic.name: Layered Artifact Generation
core_logic.description: Three-layer artifact generation: Base (always), Module (conditional on detection), Hierarchy (conditional on groups/domains). Follows Core+Extended skill layering with 5 universal skills plus conditional extended skills.
core_logic.business_impact: Generates contextually appropriate documentation artifacts based on project analysis

core_logic.name: Tiered Provider Routing
core_logic.description: Routes LLM requests to different model tiers (fast/default/performance) based on pipeline phase. Includes circuit breaker for resilience, budget tracking with lock-free atomics, and retry configuration.
core_logic.business_impact: Optimizes API costs and latency by routing requests to appropriate model tiers

core_logic.name: Circuit Breaker for Provider Resilience
core_logic.description: Tracks consecutive failures and blocks requests when threshold exceeded. Automatically recovers after cooldown period. Integrated with provider chain for failover.
core_logic.business_impact: Prevents cascading failures when LLM providers experience issues, maintaining system stability

core_logic.name: Schema-Driven Response Validation
core_logic.description: Transforms JSON schemas for strict structured output, adding additionalProperties:false and converting oneOf to Claude-compatible formats. Includes robust preprocessing pipeline for LLM output.
core_logic.business_impact: Ensures generated content conforms to expected schemas, reducing downstream errors

core_logic.name: Quality Loop with Feedback
core_logic.description: Iterative refinement loop with evidence feedback. Retries up to max_retries until target_refs met. Each iteration calls LLM to enhance content. Includes selective judgment caching for unmodified artifacts.
core_logic.business_impact: Ensures artifact quality improves iteratively within budget and time constraints

core_logic.name: Priority-Ordered Rule Generation
core_logic.description: Generates rules from 3-tier hierarchy (Domain→Groups→Modules) with priority-based ordering (100=project, 90=tech, 85=framework, 80=module, 75=domain, 70=group).
core_logic.business_impact: Generates hierarchical rules that reflect actual codebase organization and domain boundaries

workflows.name: Documentation Generation Pipeline
workflows.description: Main documentation generation workflow that orchestrates multi-phase analysis, validation, and artifact creation to produce comprehensive project documentation from source code

steps.name: Configuration Loading
steps.action: Load and merge configuration from defaults, global, project, and environment sources

steps.name: Project Detection
steps.action: Detect project type, technologies, frameworks using multi-strategy detection with file patterns and content analysis

steps.name: Constraint Extraction
steps.action: Extract constraints, conventions, and patterns from codebase via semantic routing to relevant analyzers

steps.name: Deep Analysis
steps.action: Perform distributed chunk analysis with checkpointing, AST enrichment, and LLM-based extraction
conditions: Large codebase triggers chunked parallel analysis

steps.name: Cross Synthesis
steps.action: Aggregate chunk results using map-reduce pattern to produce unified analysis findings

steps.name: Validation
steps.action: Run two-pass validation: programmatic checks followed by LLM semantic validation

steps.name: Artifact Generation
steps.action: Generate layered artifacts: Core skills (5), Agents (3), Rules with priority ordering across three tiers
conditions: Evidence gates control generation based on ProjectEvidence detection

steps.name: Quality Assessment
steps.action: Evaluate artifacts using objective metrics and LLM-based semantic quality scoring

steps.name: Refinement Loop
steps.action: Iteratively improve artifacts using strategy rotation until convergence or budget exhaustion

steps.name: Output
steps.action: Write validated artifacts to configured output locations with appropriate formats
conditions: Quality thresholds met OR max iterations reached

workflows.name: Quality Refinement Loop
workflows.description: Iterative quality improvement process using multiple strategies to refine generated artifacts until quality targets are met

steps.name: Quality Assessment
steps.action: Analyze current artifact quality using multi-dimensional scoring (mistake_prevention, discoverability, artifact_fitness)

steps.name: Convergence Check
steps.action: Check if quality has stabilized or oscillation detected via hash-based proposal history

steps.name: Strategy Selection
steps.action: StrategyRotator selects appropriate strategy based on applicable_to(), priority(), and history tracking

steps.name: Strategy Execution
steps.action: Execute selected refinement strategy (evidence enhancement, specificity, etc.) with rich context

steps.name: Failure Tracking
steps.action: Track artifact/strategy pair failures; skip pairs exceeding max_failures (default 2)

steps.name: Selective Caching
steps.action: Cache judgment results for unmodified artifacts; prune invalid cache entries

workflows.name: Consensus-Based Review
workflows.description: Multi-agent consensus process where specialized agents review and approve generated artifacts with veto power for critical decisions

steps.name: Submission
steps.action: Submit artifact for review to relevant specialist agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts)

steps.name: Agent Review
steps.action: Each agent evaluates artifact based on their expertise and provides assessment

steps.name: Veto Check
steps.action: Critical agents (reviewer, architect, domain experts) can veto and block approval

steps.name: Consensus Aggregation
steps.action: Aggregate non-vetoed assessments to determine overall consensus

steps.name: Approval
steps.action: Artifact passes review and proceeds to output

steps.name: Rejection
steps.action: Artifact rejected; feedback provided for refinement
conditions: Veto issued OR consensus not met

workflows.name: Incremental Sync Pipeline
workflows.description: Incremental update process that tracks changes and regenerates only affected artifacts based on dependency relationships

steps.name: Change Detection
steps.action: Use Blake3 hashing to detect which files have changed since last run

steps.name: Dependency Resolution
steps.action: DependencyGraph traces file→module→artifact relationships to identify affected artifacts

steps.name: Selective Regeneration
steps.action: Regenerate only artifacts whose dependencies changed, skipping unchanged portions

steps.name: State Update
steps.action: Update tracking state with new file hashes and timestamps

workflows.name: Checkpoint Recovery
workflows.description: Crash recovery process using checkpoints and event sourcing to resume interrupted analysis from last known good state

steps.name: Session Detection
steps.action: Check for existing session via lock file with PID and timestamp

steps.name: Lock Validation
steps.action: Validate lock file PID is still running; handle stale locks

steps.name: State Reconstruction
steps.action: Replay JSONL event log to reconstruct state via event sourcing pattern

steps.name: Config Validation
steps.action: Verify config hash matches to ensure compatible state

steps.name: Resume Processing
steps.action: Continue from last successful checkpoint with restored context

steps.name: Fresh Start
steps.action: Initialize new session with ULID-based directory and fresh event stream
conditions: No valid checkpoint OR config mismatch

workflows.name: Distributed Chunk Analysis
workflows.description: Distributed analysis of large codebases using parallel chunk processing with progress tracking and fault tolerance

steps.name: Chunk Partitioning
steps.action: Partition codebase into chunks based on file boundaries and size limits

steps.name: Parallel Analysis
steps.action: Process chunks concurrently with semaphore-bounded parallelism using JoinSet

steps.name: Chunk Checkpoint
steps.action: Save checkpoint after each chunk completes for recovery capability

steps.name: Progress Update
steps.action: Broadcast progress events via Arc<RwLock> + broadcast channel pattern

steps.name: Aggregation
steps.action: Map-reduce aggregation of chunk results via AnalysisAggregator::aggregate()

workflows.name: Validation Pipeline
workflows.description: Multi-tier validation pipeline combining fast programmatic checks with slower LLM-based semantic validation

steps.name: Static Validation
steps.action: Fast deterministic checks: file references, required sections, structure validation

steps.name: Reference Validation
steps.action: Validate file:line references against VerifiedFileRegistry with graduated status

steps.name: LLM Validation
steps.action: Semantic quality evaluation using LlmJudge for actionability, evidence, specificity

steps.name: Issue Aggregation
steps.action: Collect all issues with three-tier severity: errors (block), warnings (note), info

steps.name: Result Classification
steps.action: Classify result as Pass, PassWithWarnings, or Fail with score and issues list

steps.name: Early Rejection
steps.action: Reject early if deterministic checks fail, saving LLM API costs

workflows.name: Provider Circuit Breaker
workflows.description: LLM provider management with circuit breaker pattern, budget tracking, and tiered routing for resilient API interactions

steps.name: Request Routing
steps.action: Route request to appropriate model tier (fast/default/performance) based on phase

steps.name: Budget Check
steps.action: Verify budget available using atomic CAS operations on SharedBudget

steps.name: Circuit Check
steps.action: Check circuit breaker state; block if consecutive failures exceed threshold

steps.name: Provider Call
steps.action: Execute LLM call with retry logic based on RetryConfig

steps.name: Success Recording
steps.action: Reset failure counter, update metrics, deduct from budget

steps.name: Failure Recording
steps.action: Increment failure counter, check if threshold reached to open circuit

steps.name: Circuit Open
steps.action: Block requests for cooldown period, return cached/fallback response

steps.name: Budget Exhausted
steps.action: Terminate request, trigger graceful degradation with partial results

workflows.name: Layered Artifact Generation
workflows.description: Hierarchical artifact generation following three-layer architecture with evidence-gated conditional generation

steps.name: Core Layer Generation
steps.action: Generate 5 core skills that apply universally to any project

steps.name: Evidence Evaluation
steps.action: Evaluate ProjectEvidence to determine which extended artifacts to generate

steps.name: Module Layer Generation
steps.action: Generate module specialists and extended skills based on detection signals

steps.name: Hierarchy Layer Generation
steps.action: Generate domain experts and group-level rules based on hierarchy depth

steps.name: Priority Assignment
steps.action: Assign priority ordering: project(100), tech(90), framework(85), module(80), domain(75), group(70)

steps.name: Artifact Validation
steps.action: Run validate() on all generated artifacts, filter by error severity

policy_violations.expected_behavior: Tests must use Rust nightly toolchain exclusively. All jobs use Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with cache-on-failure: true. Security audit only runs on push events, not PRs

tier3_insights.title: CircularDependency: pipeline/analysis/reanalysis -> pipeline/analysis/synthesis
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Break cycle by introducing abstraction or inverting dependency direction between pipeline/analysis/reanalysis and pipeline/analysis/synthesis

tier3_insights.title: Router-Analysis State Synchronization Gap
tier3_insights.description: Router caches analysis state for routing decisions but must be explicitly rebuilt when synthesis or cross_insights change. If code updates analysis state without rebuilding the router, routing decisions will be based on stale data, causing insights to be misrouted or lost.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Create a wrapper type that couples analysis state mutations with automatic router invalidation, or use a builder pattern where router construction requires fresh analysis state as input.

tier3_insights.title: Budget CAS Exhaustion Under Concurrent LLM Calls
tier3_insights.description: Budget consumption uses CAS with retry limits. If concurrent requests exhaust MAX_CAS_RETRIES during high contention, budget updates silently fail. Combined with the extended context 1M token limit requiring API keys, OAuth users hitting the 200K limit may not get proper budget accounting.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Implement budget reservation before LLM calls rather than post-hoc accounting. Add monitoring for CAS failure rates and alert when approaching retry limits.

tier3_insights.title: Skill Argument Injection is Implicit Template Dependency
tier3_insights.description: Skills with argument_hint require $ARGUMENTS placeholder injection via inject_arguments_section(). This is a runtime template expansion dependency not visible in the skill definition. Skills will silently execute without arguments if the injection step is skipped or fails.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Validate at skill load time that any skill with argument_hint contains $ARGUMENTS placeholder, failing fast rather than at execution time.

tier3_insights.title: Progressive Disclosure Threshold Causes Context Bloat
tier3_insights.description: Progressive disclosure only activates for sections exceeding 50 lines (MIN_SECTION_SIZE_FOR_EXTRACTION). For documents with many sections just under this threshold, the full content is always included, potentially causing context window exhaustion when processing multiple artifacts.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Track cumulative context size across sections, not just per-section size. Apply progressive disclosure based on total document size when aggregate exceeds context budget.

tier3_insights.title: Module Path Validation Against Stale File Registry
tier3_insights.description: Module detection filters LLM output against file registry, but if the registry is stale (files deleted/moved since last sync), valid LLM-detected modules get silently dropped. The incremental sync pipeline may not invalidate module caches when files change.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Include file registry freshness timestamp in module validation. Trigger full resync when file registry age exceeds threshold or when filtered module count exceeds expected noise ratio.

tier3_insights.title: YAML Frontmatter Detection Collision with Markdown Rules
tier3_insights.description: YAML frontmatter validation using starts_with('---') can match markdown horizontal rules, potentially allowing malformed frontmatter to pass validation. Combined with the Tier1 Finding Rejection policy, this could allow findings to bypass security audit.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Use proper YAML parser for frontmatter extraction that validates complete '---' delimited blocks and rejects ambiguous horizontal rule patterns.

tier3_insights.title: Transaction UnwindSafe Requirement Masks Partial Rollbacks
tier3_insights.description: Transaction closures require UnwindSafe for panic catching and rollback. If a transaction closure captures non-UnwindSafe state (RefCell, raw pointers), panics may leave the database in an inconsistent state with SQLite's WAL mode holding partial writes.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Create transaction wrapper that only accepts closures with explicit UnwindSafe bound and logs/alerts on any caught panics before rollback.

tier3_insights.title: Quality Retention vs Improvement Delta Creates Rejection Oscillation
tier3_insights.description: Quality refinement requires both 85% retention AND 2% improvement delta. These constraints can conflict: a refinement that improves quality by 3% but only retains 80% of original content will be rejected, even though net quality increased. The loop may oscillate.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Track refinement attempt history and detect oscillation patterns. After N rejected refinements, accept the highest absolute quality version rather than continuing the loop.

tier3_insights.title: MCP Tool Name Pattern Validation Deferred to Runtime
tier3_insights.description: MCP tool names must follow mcp__<server>__<tool> pattern exactly. Tools registered with incorrect underscore count will fail at runtime, but the validation only occurs during tool invocation, not registration.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Validate MCP tool name format at registration time with compile-time macro or builder pattern that enforces the underscore structure.

tier3_insights.title: AST Line Variance Tolerance Insufficient After Checkpoint Recovery
tier3_insights.description: AST validation allows 5-line variance for references, but this tolerance compounds with code changes between analysis and validation phases. If Checkpoint Recovery restores an older analysis state after code edits, the 5-line tolerance may be insufficient, causing valid references to fail.
tier3_insights.prevention_guidance: Store source file hash alongside line references. Invalidate references when file hash changes rather than relying on line number tolerance.
